title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a fixed-frequency transmon qubit and an NV ensemble coupled to a common resonator, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe clear three-mode avoided crossings indicating strong coupling between all three components, with cooperativities exceeding 1.
conclusion: This work establishes a solid-state platform for coherent interactions between superconducting qubits and spin ensembles, enabling future quantum networking and memory applications.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resources.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: They find that many standard signatures of quantumness are recovered, and several phenomena long considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties.
conclusion: The work provides a more precise characterization of quantumness, with implications for quantum technologies and foundational studies.

title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phases that are not well understood experimentally.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting processor, the authors implement a hybrid quantum circuit with repeated measurements and conditional feedback, and characterize the resulting steady states via correlation functions and entanglement measures.
result: They observe a phase transition between a volume-law entangled phase and a disentangled phase, controlled by the measurement rate and feedback strength, consistent with theoretical predictions for monitored quantum circuits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can be used to engineer nonequilibrium phases of matter, providing a platform for studying quantum thermodynamics and information processing in open systems.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in classical systems; its quantum counterpart is of fundamental interest in non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states at different effective temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that under certain conditions, a hotter quantum system relaxes to equilibrium faster than a colder one, and they can modulate this effect by tuning system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides the first experimental evidence of the quantum Mpemba effect, opening avenues for controlling relaxation dynamics in quantum systems.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling or Markovian approximations, which are common in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors extend the Keldysh formalism to include Lindblad dissipators, introducing diagrammatic perturbation theory for dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: They derive a set of self-consistent equations for Green's functions and self-energies that incorporate both unitary and dissipative dynamics, enabling the study of non-equilibrium steady states and transient phenomena.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for analyzing quantum systems far from equilibrium, with applications to quantum thermodynamics, transport, and driven quantum matter.

title: Probing Quantum States Over Spacetime Through Interferometry
authors: Seok Hyung Lie And Hyukjoon Kwon
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie and Hyukjoon Kwon

Establishing a notion of the quantum state that applies consistently across space and time could be a crucial step toward formulating a relativistic quantum theory. We give an operational meaning to multipartite quantum states over arbitrary regions in spacetime through a causally agnostic measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a causally agnostic measurement scheme to operationally define multipartite quantum states over arbitrary spacetime regions, bridging quantum information and relativity.
motivation: Establishing a consistent notion of quantum states across spacetime is crucial for relativistic quantum theory, but current formulations lack operational meaning for states defined on spacelike or timelike separated regions.
method: The authors introduce a causally agnostic measurement framework that uses interferometry to probe quantum correlations without assuming a fixed causal structure, allowing the reconstruction of multipartite states over arbitrary spacetime regions.
result: They demonstrate that their scheme can reconstruct quantum states even when the regions are timelike separated, revealing that quantum states can be defined in a way that respects relativistic causality while capturing nonlocal correlations.
conclusion: The work provides an operational foundation for quantum states in spacetime, potentially enabling new insights into relativistic quantum information and the unification of quantum mechanics with relativity.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven optical cavity via phase space probability currents and estimates entropy production.
motivation: To experimentally observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a non-equilibrium quantum optical system, bridging quantum thermodynamics and stochastic processes.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven bistable optical cavity, combined with estimation of entropy production from stochastic trajectories.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and nonzero entropy production, demonstrating irreversibility in a quantum optical bistable system.
conclusion: Optical bistability serves as a testbed for non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and the methods can be extended to other driven-dissipative quantum systems.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies of interacting scalar fields can be computed as the free energy of replicated systems with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation of entanglement entropy from correlation functions.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but its direct calculation in interacting quantum field theories is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method to compute it using correlation functions.
method: They derive a relation between odd-order Rényi entropies and the free energy of N replicas of the system with additional quadratic couplings within the subsystem at the measurement time. This allows expressing the entropy in terms of two-point correlation functions.
result: The method is demonstrated for a free scalar field and an interacting scalar field with quartic coupling, showing that the entanglement entropy can be obtained from equal-time correlation functions, both in and out of equilibrium.
conclusion: The work provides a computationally feasible approach to compute entanglement entropy in interacting scalar field theories, bridging quantum information measures with field-theoretic calculations.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, where quantum effects play a significant role.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator coupled to a thermal bath.
result: They derive exact expressions for the cumulants of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and quantum signatures in the thermodynamic behavior.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum thermodynamics by providing a detailed analysis of fluctuations in a driven quantum system, with implications for quantum heat engine design.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, and nonreciprocal elements offer a way to control the flow of quantum correlations.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional couplers and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They identify a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementation must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols for detecting spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spin ensembles suffer from poor readout fidelity; dispersive measurements offer a non-destructive alternative with potential for quantum-limited sensitivity.
method: The authors theoretically model a cavity-based dispersive measurement of a spin ensemble, deriving the measurement imprecision and backaction, and optimizing parameters to achieve sub-SQL sensitivity.
result: They show that with appropriate cavity coupling and spin ensemble properties, the measurement can reach the standard quantum limit and even surpass it with squeezed light or other techniques.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision spin ensemble readout in solid-state quantum platforms, enabling applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, establishing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: In quantum thermodynamics, rapid work extraction protocols are desirable but the trade-off between power and efficiency is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze finite-time closed quantum dynamics using optimal control theory and derive bounds on extracted work based on quantum speed limits.
result: They obtain a general bound relating the maximum extractable work to the duration of the protocol and the energy fluctuations of the initial state.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits on work extraction in finite-time quantum processes, guiding the design of fast and efficient quantum engines.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of Rains' quantum shadow enumerators in terms of Bell measurement statistics, enabling efficient learning and experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion device.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for quantum error correction but lacked a direct physical interpretation, limiting their experimental accessibility.
method: The authors show that shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, and develop efficient learning protocols based on this connection.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the learning protocol on a trapped-ion quantum device, validating the physical interpretation and the efficiency of the approach.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract enumerator theory and experimental quantum error correction, offering new practical tools for characterizing quantum codes.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the coherent coupling via optical spectroscopy and second-order correlation measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling and low-noise optical transitions.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building scalable quantum repeaters and network nodes due to its high efficiency and coherence.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a squeezed reservoir to create and stabilize multipartite entangled states, with reconfigurable coupling patterns.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate robust entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and simulate topological matter, with high fidelity and resilience to noise.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics using hybrid spin-cavity systems, leveraging dissipation as a resource.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that recording midcircuit measurement data can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under measurements is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with midcircuit measurements and derive scaling laws for the quantum information lifetime using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that by recording measurement outcomes, the quantum information lifetime can be exponentially prolonged compared to the case without recording.
conclusion: This work provides a strategy to preserve fragile quantum information and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a superconducting qubit array with gap engineering, using radiation sources and measuring error correlations.
result: They observe that ionizing radiation causes spatially and temporally correlated phase errors, which persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts pose a significant obstacle to fault-tolerant quantum computing, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the microscopic origins of decoherence is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy on cavity-coupled erbium ions in silicon, analyzing spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms through time-resolved and temperature-dependent measurements.
result: They identify specific sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon show promise for quantum networking, but further material engineering is needed to achieve transform-limited linewidths.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable framework for generating large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging spin-photon interfaces and collective enhancement.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with sublinear overhead, scaling to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in monitored quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using statistical mechanics mappings and tensor network techniques to characterize decoding transitions.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and identify regimes where logical information is protected despite partial measurements.
conclusion: Random measurements can be beneficial for quantum error correction, offering new insights into the interplay between monitoring and code performance.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a device-independent randomness expansion protocol based on Bell inequality violation, integrating all necessary optical components on-chip.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits with a certified min-entropy, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, self-testing QRNGs.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, production-scale quantum security devices by combining self-testing protocols with integrated photonic technology.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed methods significantly reduce the number of required emitters and improve the loss tolerance of quantum repeater protocols, making them more feasible with near-term technology.
conclusion: Hierarchical tree-code generation and asymmetric design offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep spin defect in ZnO with exceptional spin properties, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are promising for scalable quantum technologies, but suitable spin defects with long coherence and high readout fidelity have been lacking.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations and experimental characterization to study a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring its electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: They find an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: Develops a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical device imperfections.
result: Provides a rigorous method to account for device imperfections in security proofs, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: The framework bridges theory and practice, making QKD security proofs more applicable to real-world devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can improve error correction efficiency.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved quantum error correction by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all basic tasks in a single device is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the performance of superconducting qubit platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable quantum communication, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan distances.
method: The review surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs against collective and coherent attacks, and experimental implementations with homodyne/heterodyne detection.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and secret key rates, with security proofs now covering finite-size effects and composable security. The review also discusses measurement-device-independent and twin-field CV-QKD variants.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with practical systems deployed in real-world networks and strong theoretical foundations.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional methods and providing new insights.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions and understand thermodynamic behavior of dynamical black holes.
method: Uses dynamical horizon framework and geometric analysis to derive a first law for non-equilibrium black holes.
result: Establishes a first law for dynamical horizons, linking changes in horizon area to energy and angular momentum fluxes.
conclusion: Black holes far from equilibrium obey a thermodynamic-like first law, supporting the universality of black hole thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Nonreciprocity Through Squeezing-Induced Symmetry Breaking
authors: B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, And F. Nori
abstract:
Author(s): B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, and F. Nori

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities can exponentially enhance reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity, providing a new principle for unidirectional signal flow.
motivation: Nonreciprocal devices are crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods face limitations in isolation and bandwidth. The authors aim to develop a more effective mechanism for enhancing nonreciprocity.
method: They establish a theoretical framework where squeezing in one cavity breaks the symmetry between two coupled cavities, leading to exponentially amplified nonreciprocity in the presence of a common reservoir.
result: The proposed mechanism yields exponential enhancement of nonreciprocity compared to conventional coupling scaling, as demonstrated through analytical and numerical calculations.
conclusion: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking offers a powerful tool for reservoir engineering, enabling high-performance nonreciprocal devices for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a noncommutative index for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, linking the transition to the noncommutativity of measurement operators.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was not well understood. The authors aim to provide an analytical understanding based on operator noncommutativity.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index defined via the algebraic structure of measurement operators and use it to characterize the entanglement phase transition in a class of measurement-only circuits.
result: They show that the noncommutative index sharply distinguishes the volume-law and area-law phases, and analytically compute the critical point for certain models.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a fundamental mechanism for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, offering a new tool for studying entanglement dynamics in quantum circuits.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaotic systems using the purity of the Choi matrix as a probe.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior of a subsystem; the authors aim to use quantum channels to fully capture reduced dynamics.
method: The authors study the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics (quantum channel) for a subsystem in a chaotic many-body system, analyzing its behavior as a function of time and system size.
result: They find that the Choi purity exhibits a universal decay and saturation behavior that reflects dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence, providing a probe of quantum chaos that is independent of initial state.
conclusion: The Choi purity is a robust, initial-state-independent probe of quantum chaos and decoherence in many-body systems, linking information-theoretic measures to thermodynamic irreversibility.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum implementation could enable efficient estimation on near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that implements a higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement, using amplitude amplification and iterative optimization.
result: The algorithm achieves a quadratic speedup over classical methods for certain states, and numerical simulations demonstrate its feasibility for small systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical quantum algorithm for entanglement estimation, bridging quantum information theory and quantum computing implementations.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve scalable OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XXZ interactions and a staggered transverse field, and show that in a rotating frame the effective Hamiltonian resembles OAT. They analyze the dynamics using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The staggered field enables OAT-like dynamics that generate scalable entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing, with performance comparable to all-to-all OAT for sufficiently large chains.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as scalable sources of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by invoking the standard composite-system axiom.
method: They assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit are consistent with the tensor-product structure when the qubit is part of a larger system, and derive the density matrix and Born's rule.
result: The theorem is proven for qubits, showing that the usual quantum formalism follows from the consistency condition.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum description of qubits, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high fidelity.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting speed. Faster storage is needed for scalable quantum networks.
method: The authors apply shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) via counter-diabatic driving to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic errors.
result: The STA protocol reduces storage time by orders of magnitude while maintaining high storage efficiency and fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-fidelity quantum memory in Rydberg systems, advancing quantum network technology.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of fundamental triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: While bipartite uncertainty relations are well-studied, tight triple uncertainty relations have lacked experimental verification, which is essential for foundational understanding and applications in quantum cryptography.
method: The authors design and implement a photonic experiment using polarization and path qubits to measure triple uncertainty relations for three mutually unbiased bases, employing weak measurements to avoid disturbance.
result: They observe tight triple uncertainty relations that saturate theoretical bounds, demonstrating the incompatibility of three observables simultaneously.
conclusion: The work provides the first experimental confirmation of fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing the understanding of quantum uncertainty and its implications for quantum information protocols.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium thermometry using the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing how degeneracy and spectral structure affect temperature sensitivity via quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Accurate temperature measurement at the quantum scale is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding how probe design affects sensitivity is key.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information for a probe modeled by the multilevel quantum Rabi model, exploring the role of energy-level degeneracy and spectral uniformity.
result: Probes with degeneracy can achieve higher sensitivity, while those with uniform spectra maintain sensitivity over a broader temperature range.
conclusion: The multilevel quantum Rabi model provides a versatile platform for quantum thermometry, with design principles that can optimize sensitivity for specific temperature regimes.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistical learning method to verify approximate k-designs using randomized measurements, reducing measurement resources.
motivation: Verifying quantum state k-designs is crucial for many quantum information tasks but typically requires many measurements; a more efficient method is needed.
method: The authors use randomized data and statistical learning to certify approximate k-designs, leveraging the structure of random ensembles to reduce the number of required measurements.
result: The method achieves efficient verification with fewer measurements than standard approaches, demonstrated on various quantum states.
conclusion: Statistical learning on randomized data provides a practical and resource-efficient way to verify approximate k-designs, benefiting quantum benchmarking and information tasks.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted state preparation and measurement devices.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement (SPAM) device to characterize and then purify noisy SPAM operations via iterative filtering or post-selection.
result: The protocol can significantly reduce SPAM errors, improving the fidelity of prepared states and measurements without requiring full quantum tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate SPAM errors, which is crucial for near-term quantum devices and quantum network applications.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing surface code stabilizer measurements for Rydberg atoms by minimizing logical errors rather than physical gate fidelity, with novel leakage suppression protocols.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires fault-tolerant error correction; surface code performance can be improved by tailoring gates to logical error rates and mitigating Rydberg leakage.
method: The authors analyze leakage propagation mechanisms in Rydberg-based stabilizer measurements and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress leakage, optimizing gates for logical error suppression.
result: They demonstrate that optimizing for logical errors significantly improves surface code thresholds and reduces logical error rates compared to conventional fidelity-optimized gates.
conclusion: The proposed leakage-suppressed protocols enable efficient fault-tolerant quantum error correction with neutral atoms, advancing practical quantum computing.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: High-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers.
motivation: To achieve high-resolution NMR of nuclear spin ensembles by leveraging NV centers for polarization and optical readout.
method: Stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field are used to resolve sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters.
result: Sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters are resolved, demonstrating high sensitivity.
conclusion: The technique enables sensitive NMR detection of nuclear spin clusters, relevant for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates gradient scalability in variational quantum algorithms, showing that avoiding barren plateaus leads to classically simulatable cost landscapes, and proposes a Taylor surrogate model to mitigate this issue.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, but recent conjectures suggest that avoiding them may lead to classical simulability, posing a scalability challenge.
method: The authors analyze the gradient scaling of VQAs and introduce a Taylor surrogate model that approximates the cost landscape to improve trainability while maintaining quantum advantage.
result: They demonstrate that the Taylor surrogate can escape the trade-off between barren plateaus and classical simulability, enabling efficient optimization for certain problem sizes.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to enhance VQA scalability, though the surrogate's effectiveness may be limited for very large systems.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a quantum computational advantage that is not only a proof-of-principle but also utilizable for practical tasks, addressing the challenge of verifying quantum advantage in noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, generating highly entangled states and performing computational tasks that are hard for classical computers.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is verifiable and utilizable, with the processor outperforming classical simulations in specific tasks related to many-body entanglement dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a clear demonstration of a practical quantum advantage in a controlled quantum system, highlighting the potential of ultracold-atom platforms for quantum information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving noise insensitivity and scalability.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks, but common-mode noise limits performance. The authors aim to develop a robust approach that is intrinsically insensitive to such noise.
method: They introduce entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are designed to be insensitive to common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase estimation protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states enable quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise, providing a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a robust method for quantum-enhanced sensing that can be implemented in noisy environments, advancing the field of quantum metrology.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors; passive schemes could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the uncorrected physical lifetime.
conclusion: Passive error correction can be effective for photon loss, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank as the minimum number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop a framework to compute it using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity and has implications for resource theories and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging, especially in finite magnetic fields.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve state-selective, low-loss imaging and loading of atoms in an optical tweezer array, leveraging EIT's narrow linewidth and reduced scattering.
result: They achieve high-fidelity (>99%) nondestructive imaging and efficient loading of atom arrays, with minimal atom loss and heating, even in the presence of magnetic fields.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical, high-performance method for neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum information processing and simulation.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing; this tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to the field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and optimal measurement strategies near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation, with examples from various many-body systems.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for surpassing classical limits, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving enables fast quantum control but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct better approximate counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and readily available upgrade for improving quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise or require long sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling device-tailored sequences that cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, scaling only with the locality k of the noise, and are demonstrated on various noise models.
