conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum devices with spatially correlated errors.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, providing a unified framework for symmetry-learning tasks.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: Introduces a scheme where multiple atomic modes are coupled to distinct cavity modes via spatial or frequency multiplexing, enabling parallel operations.
result: Demonstrates that cavity-mode multiplexing can process many atoms simultaneously without crosstalk, significantly increasing operation speed and scalability.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale cavity-enhanced quantum operations to large neutral-atom arrays, advancing quantum computing platforms.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, mapping the decoding problem to a statistical mechanics model and studying its phase transitions.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise strength, and characterize the spectral properties of the code's density matrix.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the fundamental limits of quantum error correction and suggest that random codes can achieve optimal thresholds under certain conditions.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptography protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes various quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It offers a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols, highlighting their theoretical capabilities and practical challenges in photonic systems.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography extends well beyond QKD, but many protocols have significant limitations; photonic implementations are advancing but face scalability and efficiency issues.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of quantum gravity using quantum information methods, particularly through tabletop experiments that probe the quantum nature of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed experimental setups that would detect entanglement between two probes mediated by gravity.
result: Several feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments are identified and analyzed, showing that quantum information theory can provide concrete experimental tests for quantum gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a promising path to experimentally test the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a key candidate.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a secret communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and propose a practical application for secure communication.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the exchange statistics of emergent paraparticles in topological phases and design a communication protocol that exploits these statistics.
result: Exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance achievable only in topological phases hosting such particles.
conclusion: The work provides a new application of paraparticles in quantum information and highlights their potential for secure communication.

title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with critical exceptional points governing their emergence.
motivation: Continuous time crystals are a novel non-equilibrium phase of matter, but the conditions for their appearance are not fully understood. The authors aim to provide a unified framework using PT symmetry.
method: The authors analyze a Lindblad master equation for a driven-dissipative system and map it to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. They identify exceptional points where the time-crystal phase emerges.
result: They demonstrate that the time-crystal phase corresponds to a PT-symmetric state, and the phase transition occurs at exceptional points of the effective Hamiltonian.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric perspective offers a clear criterion for the emergence of continuous time crystals, linking non-equilibrium phases to non-Hermitian physics.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: Understanding necessary conditions for directed currents in nonequilibrium systems is fundamental; the ratchet principle is widely used but may be incomplete.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying hidden conservation laws that suppress currents.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents despite symmetry breaking, refining the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of current emergence in stochastic systems, relevant to nonequilibrium thermodynamics and active matter.

title: Machine-Learned Tuning To Protected States By Probing Noise Resilience
authors: Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, And Rubén Seoane Souto
abstract:
Author(s): Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, and Rubén Seoane Souto

Protected states are promising for quantum technologies due to their intrinsic resilience against noise. However, such states often emerge at discrete points or small regions in parameter space and are, thus, difficult to find in experiments. In this Letter, we present a machine-learning method for …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256604] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning method tunes a quantum device to protected states by probing noise resilience.
motivation: Protected states are robust against noise but hard to locate in parameter space; efficient tuning is needed for practical quantum technologies.
method: The authors use a machine-learning algorithm that iteratively probes the system's noise resilience to navigate the parameter space and identify protected states.
result: The method successfully finds protected states in a simulated hybrid quantum system, demonstrating efficient tuning without prior knowledge of the system.
conclusion: Machine-learning-based tuning offers a practical approach to exploit protected states in quantum devices, enhancing their performance and reliability.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for tuning glassy dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles by controlling disorder statistics.
motivation: Understanding and controlling nonequilibrium relaxation in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework linking disorder distribution statistics (mean, variance) to relaxation dynamics, validated by exact numerical simulations.
result: They show that tuning disorder parameters can systematically control glassy relaxation, enabling programmable dynamics.
conclusion: The framework provides a new tool for engineering nonequilibrium quantum dynamics in disordered systems.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm to reduce the memory dimension of hidden Markov models using quantum singular value transformation and amplitude amplification.
motivation: Hidden Markov models often require large memory, limiting their efficiency. Quantum algorithms may offer dimension reduction by exploiting quantum parallelism.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that applies quantum singular value transformation to the transition matrix of an HMM, followed by amplitude amplification to extract a reduced model.
result: The algorithm achieves a polynomial reduction in memory dimension while preserving the output statistics, with provable guarantees on approximation error.
conclusion: Quantum dimension reduction of HMMs is feasible and can lead to more efficient quantum simulations of stochastic processes, with potential applications in quantum machine learning and time-series analysis.

title: Coupling-energy Driven Pumping Through Quantum Dots: Role Of Coherences
authors: Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, And Nikodem Szpak
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, and Nikodem Szpak

We study the impact of off-resonant tunneling and coherences on the electron pumping through quantum dots. Thereby, we focus on two electron-pump setups where lowest-order tunneling processes are suppressed and the pump is exclusively driven by modulations of the coupling energy. The first setup is …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235152] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron pumping through quantum dots driven solely by coupling energy modulations, highlighting the role of off-resonant tunneling and coherences.
motivation: Understanding quantum transport in nanoscale systems where lowest-order tunneling is suppressed, and exploring how coherences affect pumping.
method: Theoretical analysis of two quantum-dot pump setups using a master equation approach, focusing on coupling-energy-driven pumping and coherence effects.
result: Off-resonant tunneling and coherences significantly influence the pumped current, leading to non-trivial transport features.
conclusion: Coherences play a crucial role in coupling-energy-driven pumping, and the findings have implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum dot-based devices.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal phase, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay.
motivation: Understanding the formation of discrete time crystals in open systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics, and the applicability of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism in such systems was unknown.
method: The authors study a driven-dissipative model of a discrete time crystal and analyze the scaling of spatial defects and transition delay as a function of quench time, using numerical simulations.
result: They observe characteristic power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, indicating universality in the formation of dissipative discrete time crystals.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism extends to open systems forming discrete time crystals, providing a universal framework for defect formation in non-equilibrium quantum phases.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the bias in approximate MLE for energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and derives minimal-dissipation learning conditions.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and to find optimal training protocols that minimize dissipation.
method: The authors map the training dynamics of persistent chain EBMs to an overdamped Langevin system and compute the excess work using stochastic thermodynamics.
result: The bias of the approximate MLE objective is exactly the thermodynamic excess work, and minimal-dissipation learning corresponds to quasi-static training.
conclusion: Energy-based model training can be understood as a thermodynamic process, and dissipation can be minimized by controlling the learning rate schedule.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that for deterministic classical lattice systems with independent initial conditions, the time evolution of macroscopic observables is typically close to the microcanonical average, providing a rigorous justification of dynamical typicality.
motivation: Understanding how macroscopic irreversibility emerges from deterministic microscopic dynamics is a fundamental question in statistical mechanics. The paper aims to extend the concept of dynamical typicality, previously studied in quantum systems, to classical lattice systems.
method: The authors consider classical lattice systems with continuous variables and assume initial conditions are sampled from a product distribution. They use concentration of measure techniques to show that for any macroscopic observable, its time average over a finite time window is close to the microcanonical average with high probability.
result: They prove that the fraction of initial conditions for which the time evolution deviates significantly from the microcanonical average is exponentially small in the system size, establishing dynamical typicality for a broad class of classical lattice systems.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous foundation for the emergence of thermodynamic behavior in classical systems, showing that typical initial conditions lead to macroscopic observables that are well-described by equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of conserved quantities after quantum quenches, showing that fluctuations are governed by the same principles as equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is a fundamental challenge; the paper aims to extend thermodynamic fluctuation theory to quantum quenches.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of particle and energy transport in integrable systems after a quench, deriving exact results for the cumulant generating function.
result: They show that the statistics of fluctuations are described by a large deviation principle with a rate function given by the thermodynamic entropy of the generalized Gibbs ensemble, and verify their predictions with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for fluctuations in quantum quenches, bridging non-equilibrium dynamics and equilibrium thermodynamics, and provides testable predictions for experiments.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a quantum analog of classical synchronization.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in nonlinear dynamics, and its quantum counterpart is of interest for understanding collective behavior in quantum systems and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled via engineered dissipation, and the synchronized state is characterized by joint measurements revealing a fixed relative phase.
result: Clear evidence of phase-locking and frequency entrainment between the two quantum oscillators, consistent with theoretical predictions for quantum van der Pol oscillators.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates that synchronization can occur in the quantum regime, opening avenues for studying quantum nonlinear dynamics and collective phenomena.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped ions.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered dissipation to prepare arbitrary superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical nature through Wigner function tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex nonclassical states, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, including entropy accumulation and finite-size effects, to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, making high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.
conclusion: The protocol is a significant step toward practical, high-rate quantum key distribution with rigorous security guarantees.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally study a transmon qubit with a cosφ coupling element and perform numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of the readout process.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout is a promising approach for improving qubit measurement fidelity in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. The authors aim to achieve the Heisenberg limit using spin-dependent squeezing in trapped ions.
method: They generate spin-dependent squeezed states via a spin-motion coupling scheme in a trapped-ion system, then perform displacement sensing by measuring the spin state after a variable displacement.
result: The protocol achieves optimal sensitivity scaling with the squeezing parameter, approaching the Heisenberg limit for displacement estimation.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and lack scalability.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling efficient joint model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies the number and properties of spin baths in simulated and experimental NV center data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a fast, scalable tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with direct application to hybrid quantum systems like NV centers.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers, characterizing their bandwidth and saturation power through experimental measurements.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, improving performance for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for use in large-scale quantum processors, facilitating multiplexed readout and quantum networking applications.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity.
motivation: Standard quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting the performance of qudit-based quantum information processing. A more nondemolition readout is needed to preserve quantum states.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize back-action on the qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout significantly enhances the nondemolition character of measurements, making it a valuable tool for multilevel quantum systems across various platforms.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a theoretical framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, analyzing how noise affects the variance of gradients and connecting it to the expressivity of the circuit ansatz.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to non-vanishing gradients under certain conditions. Quantitative estimates for the loss function concentration are provided.
conclusion: The work provides a principled roadmap for navigating barren plateaus by leveraging noise, guiding the design of trainable variational quantum algorithms.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical proposal for a tunable single-photon router using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides.
motivation: To design a controllable quantum photonic routing device that can direct single photons between two output ports with high fidelity and tunability.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems (forming an effective giant atom) coupled to two waveguides, and analyze single-photon transport using a real-space approach and master equation.
result: The device functions as a tunable router: by adjusting the interatomic coupling and detuning, the photon can be directed to either waveguide with high efficiency, and the routing behavior depends on the giant-atom size.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom array provides a flexible platform for quantum photonic routing, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR) in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with independent bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as they quantify the trade-off between incompatible measurements and can be used to certify entanglement.
method: The authors model two coupled double quantum dots, each coupled to its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reservoir, and derive the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using the von Neumann entropy of the post-measurement states.
result: They find that the entropic uncertainty and its lower bound depend on the coupling strength between the dots, the reservoir temperature, and the initial state, and that the QMA-EUR can be violated under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamics of quantum correlations and uncertainty in solid-state systems, which may be relevant for quantum memory and cryptography applications.

title: Spin Model For Quantum Annealing With Kerr Parametric Oscillators
authors: Leo Stenzel, Roeland Ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Leo Stenzel, Roeland ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, and Wolfgang Lechner

Coherent states offer a promising path for near-term quantum computing due to their inherent protection against bit-flip noise. However, their large photon numbers can be challenging for numerical simulation. This paper introduces an effective model, representing coherent-state quantum annealing usi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062621] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an effective spin model for quantum annealing using Kerr parametric oscillators, enabling efficient simulation of coherent-state quantum annealing.
motivation: Coherent states offer protection against bit-flip noise but are challenging to simulate due to large photon numbers; an effective model is needed to study their quantum annealing performance.
method: The authors derive an effective spin model that maps the dynamics of Kerr parametric oscillators to a transverse-field Ising model, capturing the essential physics while reducing computational complexity.
result: The effective model accurately reproduces the annealing dynamics and ground-state properties of the original system, validated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: The spin model provides a practical tool for analyzing quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators, facilitating the design of near-term quantum annealing devices.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Wen-Jie Zhang And Jun-Hong An
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jie Zhang and Jun-Hong An

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how non-Markovian environments protect quantum steering ellipsoids, a geometric representation of steerable states.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric view of quantum correlations, but realistic environments cause decoherence. Understanding how non-Markovian effects can preserve these ellipsoids is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of quantum steering ellipsoids for two qubits coupled to independent non-Markovian environments, using exact master equations and deriving the evolution of the ellipsoid parameters.
result: They find that non-Markovian environments can significantly protect the volume and shape of steering ellipsoids compared to Markovian environments, and that memory effects can even revive steering ellipsoids after they have shrunk.
conclusion: Non-Markovian environments can be beneficial for preserving quantum steering correlations, which may have implications for quantum communication and cryptography protocols relying on steering.

title: Four-state Discrimination For A Pair Of Spin Qubits Via Gate Reflectometry
authors: Aritra Sen And András Pályi
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Sen and András Pályi

Single-electron spin qubits defined in quantum dots are used as building blocks of a semiconductor-based quantum computer. Readout in a scaled-up version of such a quantum computer is expected to rely on the Pauli spin blockade (PSB) mechanism. A desired functionality of PSB readout is that it revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235435] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gate reflectometry method to discriminate four spin states of a double quantum dot, enabling high-fidelity readout for spin qubits.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing with spin qubits requires fast and accurate readout; Pauli spin blockade readout is limited to two-state discrimination, motivating a method to distinguish all four spin states.
method: The authors model a double quantum dot coupled to a resonant circuit and analyze the reflected signal phase shift for each of the four two-electron spin states, using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the four states produce distinct phase shifts, allowing discrimination with fidelity exceeding 99% under realistic parameters.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry can be extended to four-state discrimination, offering a practical readout scheme for spin qubit arrays.

title: Distinction Between The Quantum Two-level System Relaxation Time ${t}_{1}$ And The Effective Lifetime In Single-shot Readouts
authors: Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, And Bhaskaran Muralidharan
abstract:
Author(s): Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, and Bhaskaran Muralidharan

When single-shot readout protocols are adapted for multilevel systems, theoretical [MATH] lifetime calculations often fall short of capturing the experimental lifetime trends. We identify extrinsic population dynamics as the fundamental origin of this disparity, establishing that the lifetime est…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245431] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper distinguishes between the intrinsic relaxation time T1 and the effective lifetime in single-shot readouts of quantum two-level systems, attributing discrepancies to extrinsic population dynamics.
motivation: Single-shot readout protocols for multilevel systems often yield lifetime estimates that do not match theoretical T1 calculations, hindering accurate characterization of qubit coherence.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating extrinsic population dynamics and validate it against experimental data from quantum dot or similar qubit systems.
result: They show that the effective lifetime extracted from single-shot readouts can significantly differ from T1 due to measurement-induced or environmental population redistribution.
conclusion: Careful modeling of extrinsic dynamics is necessary to correctly interpret readout lifetimes, which is crucial for assessing qubit performance in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems using generalized spin-wave approximations.
motivation: Open quantum spin systems are important for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, but exact solutions are often intractable; a scalable semiclassical method is needed.
method: The authors develop generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to quantum trajectories from the master equation, extending beyond the reaction coordinate method.
result: The framework accurately captures dissipative dynamics and steady states in regimes where standard methods fail, as demonstrated on benchmark models.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics in spin systems, relevant to quantum thermal machines and information thermodynamics.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, through active fluctuations.
motivation: The ratchet principle is a cornerstone for understanding directed transport in non-equilibrium systems, but its applicability to active matter and systems with non-thermal fluctuations is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic dynamics with asymmetric potentials and compare passive (thermal) and active (non-thermal) noise sources, using theoretical models and simulations.
result: They demonstrate that active fluctuations can break detailed balance and produce directed currents even when all symmetries are preserved, challenging the traditional ratchet principle.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be generalized to account for non-thermal fluctuations, which has implications for designing nanoscale motors and understanding biological transport.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost, using stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can localize near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant for biological and artificial swimmers.
method: The authors model the swimmer's dynamics as a stochastic process and derive optimal control strategies that minimize a cost function combining accuracy and energy expenditure.
result: They find that the optimal strategy involves a trade-off between passive drifting and active swimming, with accuracy coming at a thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the fundamental limits of localization in noisy environments, with implications for active matter and thermodynamic efficiency.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of different state preparation protocols for topological states, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: Numerical study of two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath, the other on engineered dissipation.
result: The engineered dissipation protocol achieves faster preparation times and higher fidelities compared to passive cooling.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation is a more efficient method for preparing topologically nontrivial states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and state engineering.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum self-oscillatory phases and topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems.
motivation: Understanding quantum dynamical signatures of classical bifurcations and global phase space rearrangements in open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze a driven-dissipative quantum system using phase space methods and identify topological flow transitions via quantum fluctuations.
result: They find that quantum noise can induce or suppress topological flow transitions, leading to distinct quantum limit cycle phases.
conclusion: Quantum effects fundamentally alter the classical picture of flow transitions, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control of dissipative systems.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are important in many quantum systems but are computationally challenging to simulate; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a practical and scalable method for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential for further development.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and fluctuation theorems in the continuum limit.
result: Unifies previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables in systems with both diffusive and jump-like dynamics.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics in complex systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage to highly excited states.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing leakage errors in superconducting qubits.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize the excited-state dynamics of transmon qubits, identifying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They observe and quantify the ionization process, showing how qubits escape the computational subspace through multiphoton transitions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, which can inform better readout and error mitigation strategies for superconducting quantum processors.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing time and thermalization time in quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite for chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and have implications for digital quantum simulation.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics with high configurability using photonic hardware.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling a configurable photonic simulator.
result: Demonstrates efficient execution of simulation algorithms for a large class of quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical platform for studying quantum field theories.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging. The authors aim to optimize pulses to enable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, considering experimental constraints and crosstalk.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates, advancing neutral-atom platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice to represent ancillary degrees of freedom, combined with moment-matching techniques to approximate the target nonunitary evolution.
result: The proposed method achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient approach for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum information processing and quantum simulation.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts of qubit states to measure noise cross-correlations across a range of frequencies.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, which was previously inaccessible.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, aiding in the development of more coherent quantum devices.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics in time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, enabling extrapolation beyond training data.
result: The method accurately predicts Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth for various driven quantum systems.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator through tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, advancing hybrid quantum systems for precision measurement.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized time evolution, where the Hamiltonian simulation is performed using randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, reducing the effective circuit depth.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, while maintaining the same accuracy.
conclusion: Partially randomized product formulas provide a practical and efficient approach to Hamiltonian simulation in phase estimation, making quantum chemistry simulations more feasible on near-term quantum devices.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in quantum processors, especially for near-term devices where non-Markovian and correlated noise is significant.
method: The authors develop a comprehensive noise model that captures spatiotemporally correlated errors using a sparse representation, and validate it as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used as a proxy simulator.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, enabling better error mitigation and algorithm performance.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates leakage-protected idle operation of a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to equal values, creating an energy gap that suppresses leakage errors.
motivation: Leakage errors are a major obstacle for spin qubit quantum computing; protecting idle qubits from leakage is crucial for high-fidelity operations.
method: The authors tune the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, which opens an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels, thereby suppressing leakage during idle periods.
result: They achieve leakage-protected idle operation, demonstrating reduced leakage errors in a triangular exchange-only spin qubit.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method to protect idle spin qubits from leakage, improving qubit performance.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many scientific and engineering problems, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum signal processing, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, compares their query complexities, and discusses applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and noise.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The paper highlights commonalities and differences among methods, and provides guidance for choosing appropriate simulation techniques for different physical contexts.
conclusion: Non-Markovian open quantum system dynamics can be effectively simulated using a variety of methods, each with strengths depending on the system and environment properties.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: Provides a systematic classification that guides future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum algorithms, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques (e.g., using qutrits for Toffoli gates), and experimental implementations.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates, such as the Toffoli gate with a single qutrit, and have been demonstrated in various experimental platforms.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for reducing circuit depth and improving fidelity in near-term devices.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies.
