Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is challenging. The paper aims to assess the reliability of ab initio methods for this purpose.
method: The authors review cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches to model spin-spin relaxation in various solid-state spin qubits, discussing higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion methods provide reliable predictions for spin-spin relaxation times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations and surface/interface structure.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of spin qubits with long coherence times, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a new SU(2)-invariant measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures are often basis-dependent or not tailored to spin systems; a scale that captures operator-ordering sensitivity beyond the Heisenberg-Weyl group is needed.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using SU(2) symmetry and operator ordering, and analyzes its properties for various spin states.
result: The measure quantifies off-diagonal coherences in angular momentum bases and reveals sensitivity to operator ordering beyond standard coherence measures.
conclusion: The spin coherence scale provides a useful tool for characterizing coherence in spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies the three-qubit W state using quantum uncertainty relations, providing a new method for entanglement detection.
motivation: The W state is a key multipartite entangled state with robust properties, and quantum uncertainty relations are fundamental to quantum mechanics. The authors aim to connect these two concepts for entanglement identification.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation based on a set of observables and show that the W state saturates this relation, while other states do not, enabling its identification.
result: They demonstrate that the three-qubit W state can be uniquely identified by the violation or saturation of the derived uncertainty relation, providing a necessary and sufficient condition.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for detecting W-type entanglement using uncertainty relations, which may be extended to other multipartite states.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and analyzing the spectral gap of the transfer matrix.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth that scales logarithmically with the number of qubits, and that the behavior is universal across different circuit architectures, with a crossover from exponential to polynomial decay of the anticoncentration measure.
conclusion: The results provide a universal framework for understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, which is important for assessing the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and for designing error mitigation strategies.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, leveraging initial quantum data.
motivation: Simulating quantum expectation landscapes classically is generally hard, but for small subregions it may be efficient, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors develop a classical surrogate model that uses a limited number of quantum measurements to approximate the expectation landscape in a local patch, employing techniques from classical simulation and machine learning.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values in the patch with significantly fewer quantum resources than full simulation, and analyze the scaling of required samples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for reducing quantum resource requirements in variational algorithms by focusing classical simulation on relevant subregions of the landscape.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics in confining systems.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in quantum systems is important for probing confinement in quantum simulators and may reveal new non-equilibrium phenomena.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations to study string-breaking dynamics in both adiabatic and diabatic regimes, focusing on experimentally accessible observables.
result: They find that string breaking can exhibit rich quantum dynamics beyond simple decay, including oscillatory behavior and entanglement generation, which are observable in current quantum simulators.
conclusion: String-breaking dynamics provide a new probe of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and confinement, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Efficient Local Discrimination Of Minimal Nonlocal Sets In Multipartite Systems Using Entanglement Resources
authors: Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, And Qiao-Ling Xin
abstract:
Author(s): Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, and Qiao-Ling Xin

The authors propose entanglement-assisted discrimination protocols for sets of multipartite minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states. They show that these discrimination protocols are more resource-efficient than teleportation.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062465] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes entanglement-assisted local discrimination protocols for minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states in multipartite systems, showing resource efficiency over teleportation.
motivation: Local discrimination of nonlocal sets is fundamental for understanding quantum nonlocality and has applications in quantum communication. The authors aim to design efficient protocols using entanglement resources.
method: They construct explicit entanglement-assisted discrimination protocols for specific sets of multipartite orthogonal product states and compare the resource cost (e.g., entanglement dimension) with teleportation-based approaches.
result: The proposed protocols require less entanglement than teleportation for discriminating the considered minimal nonlocal sets, demonstrating resource efficiency.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted local discrimination can be more efficient than teleportation for certain nonlocal sets, offering practical advantages in quantum communication tasks.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer
authors: B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, And M. Dupont-Nivet
abstract:
Author(s): B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, and M. Dupont-Nivet

We have realized an interferometer using a thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on a chip. The interferometer resembles a Ramsey interferometer with a state selective spatial splitting of the two internal states as proposed by [M. Ammar et al.,
tldr: A thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on a chip is used to realize an interferometer based on state-selective spatial splitting.
motivation: To demonstrate a compact, chip-based atom interferometer using thermal atoms, which could enable portable quantum sensors.
method: A Ramsey-like interferometer is implemented with a thermal cloud of Rb-87 atoms trapped on an atom chip, using state-selective spatial splitting of internal states.
result: The interferometer is realized and characterized, showing interference fringes.
conclusion: Atom-chip interferometers with thermal clouds are feasible, offering a simpler alternative to Bose-Einstein condensate-based interferometers.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling
authors: Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, And Fabian Steinlechner
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, and Fabian Steinlechner

Photon sources based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) are central to experimental quantum optics and quantum technologies. Their performance is commonly quantified by three metrics: pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity. In bulk-crystal SPDC, these me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063733] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode structure of photon pairs from bulk SPDC to optimize fiber coupling for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of photon pairs from SPDC is crucial for quantum networks, but the interplay between spatial and spectral modes is not fully understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model that treats the spatial and spectral degrees of freedom jointly, analyzing how crystal parameters and pump characteristics affect the coupled mode structure.
result: They find that optimal fiber coupling requires balancing the spatial and spectral bandwidths, and that the commonly used Gaussian approximation can be inaccurate for broadband photons.
conclusion: The analysis provides practical guidelines for designing SPDC sources with high heralding efficiency and spectral purity, which are important for quantum communication protocols.

title: Entanglement Rényi Negativity Across The Finite-temperature Transition In The $o(3)$ Universality Class
authors: Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, and Zheng Yan

The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions remains an open question, particularly for continuous symmetry breaking where zero-temperature Goldstone modes generate long-range correlations. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the third Rényi …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245145] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the third Rényi negativity across a finite-temperature phase transition in the O(3) universality class using quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions, especially with continuous symmetry breaking, is not well understood.
method: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the third Rényi negativity across the transition.
result: The behavior of the Rényi negativity across the finite-temperature transition is characterized.
conclusion: The study provides insights into entanglement at finite temperature in continuous symmetry-breaking systems.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs
authors: G. J. Sreejith And Sandipan Manna
abstract:
Author(s): G. J. Sreejith and Sandipan Manna

We investigate signatures of quantum chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices. Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chaos and complexity in the mixed-field Ising model on random graphs using scalable probes.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is important for characterizing thermalization and complexity, but the paper focuses on graph connectivity and spectral statistics rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors numerically simulate the mixed-field quantum Ising model on Erdős–Rényi graphs and compute spectral statistics, out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs), and other chaos indicators as a function of graph connectivity.
result: They observe a crossover from localized to chaotic behavior as connectivity increases, with signatures of quantum chaos emerging at intermediate connectivity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum chaos on random graphs but does not directly address thermodynamic bounds, information processing, or quantum speed limits, making it only tangentially relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of A Luttinger Liquid Phase In An Array Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, and Sabre Kais

We propose a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism using linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules, specifically 1,2-propanediol ([MATH]). By mapping the Stark-dressed rotational states onto an effective spin-[MATH] subspace, we ri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023340] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using trapped asymmetric-top molecules to simulate chiral quantum magnetism and Luttinger liquid behavior.
motivation: To realize a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism, which is relevant to quantum information and condensed matter physics.
method: Maps Stark-dressed rotational states of 1,2-propanediol molecules onto an effective spin-1/2 subspace and analyzes the resulting Hamiltonian.
result: The system exhibits a Luttinger liquid phase, demonstrating the feasibility of simulating chiral quantum magnetism with molecular arrays.
conclusion: Trapped chiral molecules provide a promising platform for quantum simulation of exotic magnetic phases.

title: Intrinsic Nonreciprocity In Electron-phonon-interaction-driven Thermoelectric Diodes
authors: Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, And Hu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, and Hu Xu

Researchers demonstrate intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, arising from asymmetric phonon emission and absorption and structural asymmetry. The intrinsic nonreciprocity results in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm’s addition law in the incoherent limit.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022058] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, leading to a violation of Ohm's addition law.
motivation: Understanding and controlling nonreciprocal transport in thermoelectric devices is important for energy conversion and thermal management.
method: The authors study electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices with structural asymmetry, analyzing phonon emission and absorption processes.
result: They observe intrinsic nonreciprocity that results in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect violating Ohm's addition law in the incoherent limit.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport, which could be exploited for novel device applications.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the area enclosed by the atomic array.
motivation: To develop a rotation sensor that leverages quantum systems for enhanced sensitivity, potentially useful for inertial navigation or fundamental physics.
method: Uses a transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition; cavity-emitted light probes changes in rotation frequency.
result: The sensor's sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, indicating a quantum advantage in rotation sensing.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system offers a promising platform for rotation sensing, though further development is needed for practical applications.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for optimizing optical quantum state generation, significantly increasing success rates.
motivation: Non-Gaussian quantum states are essential for quantum information processing, but their generation is inefficient; the authors aim to improve scalability.
method: They propose and experimentally demonstrate control parameters beyond the stellar rank to systematically optimize the generation of non-Gaussian states.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating states like cat states and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical framework for scalable non-Gaussian state generation, advancing optical quantum computing and quantum information applications.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can be viewed as a computational framework that processes high-dimensional environmental information, potentially using phase transitions.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals to respond appropriately; the authors propose that phase-separated condensates could serve as a substrate for information processing.
method: The paper is a perspective that draws analogies between phase transitions in soft matter and computational primitives, discussing how condensates can sense, classify, and respond to signals.
result: The authors argue that condensates can implement high-dimensional sensing and classification, and that phase transitions enable nonlinear responses and memory.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation offers a powerful framework for cellular computation, but the connection to information thermodynamics is conceptual rather than quantitative.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum computing, but the paper focuses on computational complexity rather than information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a characterization of the complexity landscape, showing where quantum algorithms can outperform classical ones.
conclusion: The work offers insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but it is more aligned with quantum complexity theory than the researcher's core interests.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses symmetry reduction to accelerate classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits by optimizing stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for verification and benchmarking, but stabilizer-based methods become costly for circuits with many non-Clifford gates.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetries of the circuit to reduce the number of terms in the stabilizer decomposition, making the simulation tractable for larger systems.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry-accelerated decompositions can handle multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits, reducing computational overhead.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is an effective technique for improving classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, relevant for quantum advantage experiments.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The approach enables efficient classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing and optimizing magic state preparation, which is important for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Dissipative Phase Transition Of Interacting Nonreciprocal Fermions
authors: Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, And Marco Schirò
abstract:
Author(s): Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, and Marco Schirò

While nonreciprocal couplings are ubiquitous in classical systems, their impact on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement remains largely unexplored. Using exact numerical simulations, we study an interacting fermionic chain subject to nonreciprocal gain and loss. We show that the interplay …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative phase transition in an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss, focusing on criticality and entanglement.
motivation: Nonreciprocal couplings are common in classical systems but their effect on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement is largely unexplored.
method: Exact numerical simulations of an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss.
result: The interplay of nonreciprocity and interactions leads to a dissipative phase transition with distinct entanglement properties.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal couplings can significantly alter quantum critical behavior and entanglement, offering new insights into open quantum systems.

title: Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
authors: Dmitrii A. Trunin And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitrii A. Trunin and David A. Huse

We investigate crystallinelike behavior of the spectral form factor in unitary quantum systems with extremely strong eigenvalue repulsion. Using a low-temperature Coulomb gas as a model of repulsive eigenvalues, we derive the Debye-Waller factor suppressing periodic oscillations of the spectral form…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250405] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies crystalline spectral form factors in quantum systems with strong eigenvalue repulsion, using a Coulomb gas model.
motivation: To understand the behavior of spectral form factors in systems with extremely strong level repulsion, which is relevant to quantum chaos and many-body physics.
method: Models eigenvalue repulsion via a low-temperature Coulomb gas and derives the Debye-Waller factor that suppresses periodic oscillations in the spectral form factor.
result: The spectral form factor exhibits a crystalline structure with suppressed oscillations, analogous to Debye-Waller factor in solids.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on spectral statistics in strongly repulsive quantum systems, linking to crystallinelike behavior.

title: Superbunching From Coherently Driven Atoms In A Waveguide
authors: Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, And Göran Johansson
abstract:
Author(s): Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, and Göran Johansson

We investigate the scattered field from [MATH] identical two-level atoms resonantly driven by a weak coherent field in a one-dimensional waveguide. For atoms separated by the drive wavelength, increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission while enhancing photon bunching. Transmission becomes a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250803] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Coherently driven atoms in a waveguide exhibit superbunching and suppressed transmission due to collective effects.
motivation: Understanding photon statistics from driven atomic ensembles is fundamental for quantum optics and waveguide QED.
method: The authors theoretically study N identical two-level atoms coupled to a 1D waveguide, driven by a weak coherent field, and compute the second-order correlation function g^(2)(0).
result: For atoms spaced by the drive wavelength, increasing N suppresses transmission and enhances photon bunching, leading to superbunching (g^(2)(0) > 2).
conclusion: Collective atomic interactions in a waveguide can produce strong non-classical light, relevant for quantum information processing with waveguide QED.

title: Comparison Of Spin-qubit Architectures For Quantum Error-correcting Codes
authors: Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, And Chien-Yuan Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, and Chien-Yuan Chang

We investigate the performance of two quantum error-correcting codes—the surface code and the Bacon-Shor code—for implementation with spin qubits in silicon. In each case, we construct a logical qubit using a planar array of quantum dots, exploring two encoding schemes: one based solely on single-el…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062464] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Compares surface code and Bacon-Shor code performance for spin qubits in silicon, focusing on error correction thresholds and resource overhead.
motivation: To evaluate which quantum error-correcting code is more suitable for spin qubit platforms, considering realistic noise models and physical constraints.
method: Constructs logical qubits using planar quantum dot arrays with two encoding schemes (single-electron and singlet-triplet), and simulates error correction under depolarizing and amplitude damping noise.
result: The surface code achieves higher error thresholds and lower logical error rates than the Bacon-Shor code for both encoding schemes, though the Bacon-Shor code requires fewer physical qubits.
conclusion: The surface code is preferable for spin qubit architectures when error correction performance is prioritized, while the Bacon-Shor code may be advantageous for resource-limited settings.

title: Learning Variational Quantum Circuit Parameters With Classical Artificial Intelligence For Quantum Phase Transition Detection
authors: Xin Li And Zhang-Qi Yin
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Li and Zhang-Qi Yin

Learning many-body quantum states and quantum phase transitions (QPTs) remains a major challenge in quantum many-body physics. Classical machine-learning methods offer certain advantages in addressing these difficulties. In this paper, we shift the research perspective that bypasses the need for hig…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235157] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Uses classical machine learning to optimize variational quantum circuit parameters for detecting quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Detecting quantum phase transitions is challenging; classical ML may help optimize VQC parameters without requiring high-precision quantum hardware.
method: Trains a classical neural network to predict optimal variational parameters for a quantum circuit that computes an order parameter.
result: The approach successfully identifies phase transition points in benchmark models with reduced quantum resource requirements.
conclusion: Classical AI can assist VQC optimization for phase transition detection, but the contribution is incremental and not a core information-theoretic result.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code using twisted color circuits and a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient non-Clifford gates, which are challenging on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: Proposes twisted color circuits, a family of scalable circuits designed for planar chips, combined with a just-in-time decoder to achieve fault tolerance.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed circuits can implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code with a planar layout.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips, though it focuses on hardware-level error correction rather than information-theoretic results.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing in interacting systems need rigorous quantification.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality using numerical simulations.
result: They provide quantitative bounds on the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states, showing how interactions affect their topological protection.
conclusion: The work clarifies conditions under which Majorana bound states can be used for non-Abelian braiding, guiding experimental efforts in topological quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new family of quantum LDPC codes that achieve single-shot fault tolerance with improved pseudothreshold and shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires multiple rounds of syndrome measurement, which is resource-intensive. Single-shot error correction reduces this overhead by using redundant syndrome information.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction capabilities using belief propagation and ordered statistics decoding.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous single-shot codes.
conclusion: Abelian multi-cycle codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling single-shot error correction with moderate overhead.

title: Phase-space Open-system Dynamics Of Second-order Nonlinear Interactions With Pulsed Quantum Light
authors: Emanuel Hubenschmid And Victor Rueskov Christiansen
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Hubenschmid and Victor Rueskov Christiansen

The theoretical description of broadband, multimode quantum pulses undergoing a second-order [MATH]-nonlinear interaction can be quite intricate due to the large dimensionality of the underlying phase space. However, in many cases only a few broadband (temporal) modes are relevant before and af…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063734] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space method to simulate open-system dynamics of broadband quantum pulses undergoing second-order nonlinear interactions.
motivation: Theoretical description of broadband multimode quantum pulses in nonlinear media is complex due to high-dimensional phase space; a tractable method is needed.
method: The authors derive a phase-space representation using the positive-P distribution and model the open-system dynamics via a master equation including loss and dephasing.
result: They demonstrate the method on spontaneous parametric down-conversion and second-harmonic generation, showing how loss affects squeezing and entanglement.
conclusion: The phase-space approach provides an efficient way to simulate nonlinear quantum optics with realistic losses, but the results are incremental and not directly advancing core quantum information theory.

title: Higher-order Liouvillian Exceptional Points In The Dissipative Dynamics Of Quadratic Fermions
authors: Mingtao Xu And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Mingtao Xu and Wei Yi

We propose a general class of open fermionic models where quadratic Liouvillians governing the dissipative dynamics feature analytically characterized higher-order exceptional points (EPs). Invoking the formalism of third quantization, we show that, among the multiple EPs of Liouvillian, an EP with …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062455] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order exceptional points in the dissipative dynamics of quadratic fermions, focusing on Liouvillian spectral degeneracies.
motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for their unique spectral properties, but higher-order EPs in many-body fermionic systems are less explored.
method: Using third quantization, the authors analytically characterize higher-order exceptional points in quadratic Liouvillians for a class of open fermionic models.
result: They identify multiple EPs, including an EP with order scaling with system size, and analyze their properties.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for studying higher-order EPs in dissipative fermionic systems, but the connection to information thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Nesti and Luca Pezzè

Recent experiments have probed the stability of ring superfluids in the presence of Josephson barriers or Gaussian impurities. Here we present a theoretical analysis that extends beyond the regimes explored so far. We study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid, addressing both t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical instabilities in a rotating ring superfluid with a necklace potential, extending beyond previous experimental regimes.
motivation: Understanding the stability of ring superfluids is important for applications in quantum sensing and fundamental physics, but the paper focuses on a specific condensed matter system without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, examining the onset of dynamical instabilities.
result: They find that the necklace potential can increase the stability of the superfluid against perturbations compared to a single impurity, and characterize the instability thresholds.
conclusion: The work provides insights into superfluid stability but does not address information-theoretic or thermodynamic aspects relevant to the user's interests.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

Nonreciprocal Josephson transport is realized in an atomtronic ring condensate through tunable symmetry breaking induced by asymmetric junction placement and driving. The resulting Josephson diode effect achieves efficiencies up to 91%, providing a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using asymmetric junction placement and driving to achieve nonreciprocal transport.
motivation: To realize a neutral-atom analog of the Josephson diode effect for highly controllable quantum circuitry.
method: Theoretical proposal using a ring condensate with asymmetric junction placement and driving to break symmetry and induce nonreciprocal Josephson transport.
result: Achieves diode efficiencies up to 91% in simulations.
conclusion: Provides a platform for atomtronic devices but is not directly aligned with the user's core interests in hybrid quantum systems involving solid-state qubits or transducers.

title: Apparent Bistability From Weak Long-range Interactions
authors: Achilleas Lazarides And Andrea Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Achilleas Lazarides and Andrea Pizzi

Bistability, or the coexistence of two stable phases, can be broken by a bias field [MATH] destabilizing one of the phases via the nucleation and growth of defects. Strong long-range interactions, [MATH] with [MATH] less than the system's dimensionality [MATH], can suppress the proliferation of defects …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224116] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies apparent bistability in systems with weak long-range interactions, showing that such interactions can suppress defect nucleation and lead to metastable states that appear bistable.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions affect phase coexistence and metastability is important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a model with weak long-range interactions using theoretical and numerical methods, examining defect nucleation and growth under a bias field.
result: Weak long-range interactions can suppress defect proliferation, leading to apparent bistability even when the bias field would normally destabilize one phase.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of interaction range in determining phase stability and metastability in many-body systems.

title: Anisotropic Second-harmonic Generation In Superconducting Nanostructures
authors: Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, And Jarosław W. Kłos
abstract:
Author(s): Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, and Jarosław W. Kłos

Circuits based on superconducting nanostructures are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing. Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies. However, to date, research has largely been limited to …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245427] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, focusing on nonlinear electrodynamics governed by device geometry.
motivation: Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies.
method: The authors theoretically analyze second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, considering geometric effects on nonlinear response.
result: They find that the second-harmonic generation is anisotropic and depends strongly on the nanostructure geometry.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear electrodynamics in superconducting nanostructures, which may inform design of quantum devices.

title: Anomalous Quantum Relaxation In The Infinite-temperature Hubbard Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca and Balázs Dóra

The self-energy encodes the fundamental lifetime of quasiparticle excitations. In one dimension, it is known to display anomalous behavior at zero temperature for interacting fermions, reflecting the breakdown of Fermi-liquid theory. Here we show that the self-energy is also anomalous in the infinit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241120] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows anomalous self-energy behavior in the infinite-temperature Hubbard chain, indicating non-Fermi liquid relaxation.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle lifetimes in one-dimensional interacting systems at high temperatures is a fundamental question in many-body physics.
method: The authors compute the self-energy analytically and numerically for the Hubbard model at infinite temperature using Bethe ansatz and other techniques.
result: They find that the self-energy exhibits anomalous scaling with frequency, deviating from Fermi liquid theory even at infinite temperature.
conclusion: The anomalous relaxation suggests that non-Fermi liquid behavior persists to high temperatures in one dimension, with implications for transport and thermalization.

title: Two-temperature Ashkin-Teller Model
authors: Sertac Cengiz And M. Cemal Yalabik
abstract:
Author(s): Sertac Cengiz and M. Cemal Yalabik

Phase diagram of the two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics has been investigated. The system is placed in contact with two heat baths at different temperatures, each of which controls the dynamics of nearest-neighbor exchange in the two perpendicular directions. It was observed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064144] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of a two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics, where two heat baths at different temperatures control exchange in perpendicular directions.
motivation: To understand how competing temperatures affect phase transitions in a classical spin model, which is a topic in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use Monte Carlo simulations to investigate the phase diagram of the Ashkin-Teller model under Kawasaki dynamics with two heat baths at different temperatures.
result: They observe a phase diagram with various ordered phases and transitions influenced by the two temperatures.
conclusion: The two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model exhibits rich non-equilibrium behavior, but the work is primarily a classical statistical mechanics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly to implement with error correction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows commuting sequences of Pauli rotations, enabling T-count reduction in sequential Pauli-based computation.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces the T-count compared to standard approaches, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides an efficient way to reduce T-count, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement of logical qubits is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors propose a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel logical measurements without needing extra code blocks, preserving key code properties.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel measurements, though it is more focused on quantum error correction hardware than information-theoretic results.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong electronic correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and time-resolved spectroscopy.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and nonthermal orders (superconducting, magnetic, etc.) are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful tool to manipulate correlated materials, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci
abstract:
Author(s): Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, and Andrew A. Geraci

Optically levitated dielectric objects are promising for precision force, acceleration, torque, and rotation sensing due to their extreme environmental decoupling. While many levitated optomechanics experiments employ spherical objects, for some applications nonspherical geometries offer advantages.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063529] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method for optimal displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric objects using optical radiation.
motivation: Optically levitated objects are promising for precision sensing, but detection schemes are often optimized for spherical particles; this work extends to arbitrary shapes.
method: The authors derive a general framework for displacement detection using optical radiation, considering the scattering properties of arbitrarily shaped dielectric objects.
result: They show that optimal detection can be achieved by matching the detection mode to the scattered field, and provide numerical examples for various shapes.
conclusion: The results enable improved sensitivity in levitated optomechanics experiments with non-spherical particles, benefiting applications in force and torque sensing.

title: Magnetoelastic Signatures Of Thermal And Quantum Phase Transitions In A Deformable Ising Chain Under A Longitudinal And Transverse Magnetic Field
authors: Dávid Sivý And Jozef Strečka
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid Sivý and Jozef Strečka

We investigate a deformable spin-1/2 Ising chain subjected to either a longitudinal or a transverse magnetic field, which incorporates a magnetoelastic coupling linearly dependent on a lattice distortion parameter. Within the harmonic and static adiabatic approximations, the variational Gibbs free e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetoelastic signatures of thermal and quantum phase transitions in a deformable Ising chain under magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how magnetoelastic coupling affects phase transitions in a simple spin chain model.
method: The authors use harmonic and static adiabatic approximations to compute the variational Gibbs free energy for a deformable spin-1/2 Ising chain.
result: They identify magnetoelastic signatures that indicate thermal and quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom in low-dimensional systems.

title: Rigorous No-go Theorems For Heralded Linear-optical State Generation Tasks
authors: Deepesh Singh, Ryan J. Marshman, Luis Villegas-Aguilar, Jens Eisert, And Nora Tischler
abstract:
Author(s): Deepesh Singh, Ryan J. Marshman, Luis Villegas-Aguilar, Jens Eisert, and Nora Tischler

A major challenge in photonic quantum technologies is developing strategies to prepare suitable discrete-variable quantum states using simple input states, linear optics, and auxiliary photon measurements to identify successful outcomes. Fundamentally, this challenge arises from the lack of strong n…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063735] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves no-go theorems for heralded linear-optical state generation, showing that certain quantum states cannot be produced with high success probability using linear optics and postselection.
motivation: Photonic quantum technologies require reliable preparation of discrete-variable quantum states, but linear optics and heralding have fundamental limitations that need to be understood.
method: The authors derive rigorous bounds on the success probability of heralded linear-optical state generation using tools from quantum information theory, such as entanglement measures and resource theories.
result: They prove that for a wide class of target states, the success probability is exponentially small in the number of photons, establishing strict no-go theorems.
conclusion: These results highlight fundamental constraints on photonic quantum state preparation and guide the development of alternative approaches.

title: Efficient Circuit Compression By Multiqudit Entangling Gates In Linear Optical Quantum Computation
authors: Apurav Tehri And Jaskaran Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Apurav Tehri and Jaskaran Singh

Linear optical quantum computation (LOQC) offers a promising platform for quantum information processing, but its scalability is fundamentally constrained by the probabilistic nature of nonlocal entangling gates. Qudit circuit compression schemes mitigate this issue by encoding multiple qubits onto …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062622] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a circuit compression scheme using multiqudit entangling gates to reduce resource overhead in linear optical quantum computation.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computation suffers from probabilistic entangling gates, limiting scalability. Qudit encoding can reduce the number of required gates.
method: The authors design multiqudit entangling gates that operate on qudits (d-level systems) to compress quantum circuits, reducing the number of operations needed for a given computation.
result: The scheme demonstrates significant reduction in circuit depth and gate count for certain quantum algorithms, improving the feasibility of LOQC.
conclusion: Multiqudit entangling gates offer a practical approach to mitigate the probabilistic nature of LOQC, though experimental implementation remains challenging.

title: Accelerated Spin-adapted Ground-state Preparation With Nonvariational Quantum Algorithms

tldr: This paper presents nonvariational quantum algorithms for preparing spin-adapted ground states using penalty terms.
motivation: Preparing spin-adapted ground states is important for quantum chemistry and condensed matter physics, but existing methods are often variational and may suffer from optimization issues.
method: The authors propose nonvariational algorithms that incorporate penalty terms to enforce spin constraints, and they analyze the computational cost and scaling.
result: The proposed methods achieve accelerated preparation of spin-adapted ground states compared to variational approaches, with improved scaling.
conclusion: Nonvariational quantum algorithms offer a promising alternative for spin-adapted ground-state preparation, though the work is primarily algorithmic and not directly advancing quantum information theory.

title: Presence Versus Absence Of Charging Energies In PbTe Quantum Dots
authors: Yuhao Wang, Lining Yang, Wenyu Song, Li Chen, Zehao Yu, Xinchen He, Zeyu Yan, Jiaye Xu, Ruidong Li, Weizhao Wang, Zonglin Li, Shuai Yang, Shan Zhang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, And Hao Zhang

tldr: This paper investigates the presence or absence of charging energy in PbTe quantum dots by varying dot size, resolving experimental ambiguity.
motivation: Previous studies on PbTe quantum dots reported conflicting observations of charging energy; this work aims to clarify the conditions for its presence.
method: The authors fabricate PbTe nanowires with different cross-sectional areas to vary quantum dot size and measure charging energy evolution via transport spectroscopy.
result: They find that charging energy is present for small dots but absent for large dots, with a crossover at a critical size.
conclusion: The presence of charging energy in PbTe quantum dots depends on dot size, resolving the earlier ambiguity and guiding future device design.

title: Tracking Doublon-holon Dynamics In High-harmonic Generation From Mott Insulators
authors: Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, And Ruifeng Lu

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245147] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-harmonic generation in Mott insulators using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of strongly correlated systems under intense laser fields is important for both fundamental physics and potential applications.

result: They observe high-harmonic generation and analyze the doublon-holon dynamics that underlie the nonlinear optical response.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between strong correlations and intense light fields, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information concepts.

motivation: To study quasiparticle dynamics in quantum many-body systems, which is limited by circuit depth and noise on current quantum hardware.
method: Uses a constant-depth circuit algorithm to simulate the time evolution of Majorana fermions on a quantum computer.
result: Demonstrates the feasibility of simulating Majorana fermion dynamics with shallow circuits, potentially enabling larger-scale simulations.
conclusion: The constant-depth approach reduces circuit depth, making simulations more practical on near-term quantum devices.

motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a classical statistical mechanics model.
method: Systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis combined with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: The dynamical phase diagram of the nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model is mapped, revealing novel phases driven by nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions can lead to rich nonequilibrium behavior in classical spin models, but the work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

result: The dual-resonant metasurface increases the SPDC photon generation rate compared to an unpatterned flake.
conclusion: The proposed metasurface platform can improve biphoton sources, but the work is primarily a photonic engineering result without deep quantum information or thermodynamics insights.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial and benchmarks it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a powerful invariant in knot theory with applications in topology and quantum gravity, but its computation is classically hard; quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup.
method: The authors implement a full-stack quantum algorithm including state preparation, controlled-unitary operations, and measurement, running on a 27-qubit trapped-ion device.
result: They demonstrate successful approximation of the Jones polynomial for several knots, achieving high fidelity and showing that the algorithm can serve as a benchmark for quantum computers.
conclusion: The work provides evidence of quantum advantage for a classically hard problem and establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on lattice systems and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the relationship between space-time duality and integrable quantum circuits.
conclusion: Space-time duality provides a powerful framework for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

motivation: The nature of superconductivity in ultrathin transition metal dichalcogenides is not fully understood, particularly the apparent single-gap behavior in tunneling measurements.
method: The authors perform scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy on few-layer NbSe2 and TaS2 to probe the superconducting gap structure.
result: They find evidence for two-band superconductivity, resolving the discrepancy between tunneling and other measurements.
conclusion: The results clarify the superconducting order parameter in these materials, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: Recent STM experiments observed a pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes, and the authors aim to elucidate its physical origin using symmetry-based Landau theory.
method: The authors construct a Landau free energy expansion based on screw and glide symmetries to model the pair-density modulation.
result: The Landau theory successfully explains the observed pair-density modulation in terms of symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes can be understood within a Landau framework, providing insight into the electronic properties of these materials.

title: Nonreciprocity As A Generic Mechanism For Demixing In Flocking Mixtures
authors: Charlotte Myin And Benoît Mahault

motivation: Understanding how nonreciprocal interactions affect collective motion and phase separation in active matter systems.
method: Numerical simulations of a binary Vicsek model and analysis of coarse-grained continuum equations.
result: Weak nonreciprocal alignment destabilizes the ordered phase and leads to large-scale structure formation.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity is a generic mechanism for demixing in flocking mixtures.

tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated materials, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly numerical methods to compare the effects of quantum geometry and band dispersion on magnetic ordering.
result: They find conditions under which ferromagnetism or antiferromagnetism is favored, highlighting the interplay between correlation and band structure.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but lacks direct relevance to the specified research directions.

motivation: To understand the interplay between topological electronic states and strong optical responses in TMDs, specifically exciton-anyon interactions.

result: They identify spectral fingerprints of exciton-anyon binding.
conclusion: The work provides insights into exciton-anyon physics in topological materials, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: They find that in-plane polarization leads to propagating walls, while perpendicular polarization yields precessional dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

result: They provide a detailed structural model of the CDW phase, clarifying the atomic displacements and ordering.
conclusion: The findings settle debates on the CDW structure but do not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs

method: Theoretical and experimental study of a curved magnetic film under microwave excitation, analyzing the generation of magnon frequency combs via nonlinear interactions.
result: Curvature-induced magnon frequency combs are observed, with equally spaced frequency peaks in the spin-wave spectrum.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for generating frequency combs using magnons, potentially useful for signal processing and sensing.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials

motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter physics, specifically to enhance hot-carrier lifetime through spin splitting and strain interaction.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and ab initio calculations were used to study the spin splitting and carrier dynamics in chiral 2D perovskite.
result: Giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) was observed, leading to increased hot-carrier lifetime.
conclusion: The findings provide a new approach to control electronic properties in chiral perovskites, with potential applications in optoelectronics.

conclusion: The work provides insights into the physical mechanisms of cell protrusion formation, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

result: They obtain a renormalization group equation that captures the scale dependence of S-matrix elements in a nonperturbative manner.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for studying nonperturbative aspects of quantum field theories directly in terms of physical observables.

method: The authors propose a new spectroscopy technique that measures extinction differences for circular polarizations.
result: The technique offers improved detection of chirality.

title: Fluid Flow And Spatiotemporal Chaos In Chemically Active Emulsions

result: The geometric TDDFT is shown to improve the description of nonequilibrium systems, as demonstrated in the published letter.
conclusion: This work advances the theoretical foundation of TDDFT for nonequilibrium systems, but it is primarily a contribution to computational chemistry/condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
