tldr: This paper constructs the exact BCS ground-state wave function for a p+is superconducting chain under open boundary conditions and studies its edge magnetization.
motivation: BCS wave functions under periodic boundary conditions are well known, but obtaining explicit forms under open boundary conditions is nontrivial and important for understanding edge properties.
method: The authors analytically construct the many-body BCS wave function for an open p+is superconducting chain using a Bogoliubov transformation and solve for the edge magnetization.
result: They obtain an exact expression for the ground-state wave function and compute the edge magnetization, revealing nontrivial edge physics.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for a superconducting system with open boundaries, highlighting edge effects in topological superconductors.

title: Flat-band Driven Kondo Breakdown And Reentrant Effects In Heavy-fermion Moiré Superlattices
authors: Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, and Benedikt Fauseweh

Moiré superlattices (MSLs) in van der Waals heterostructures have demonstrated their incredible power in driving emergent electronic phenomena, some of which are reminiscent of those usually only observed in bulk strongly correlated quantum materials. With the recent discovery of van der Waals [MATH]-e…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235153] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices, focusing on strongly correlated electronic phenomena.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in van der Waals heterostructures can host emergent electronic phenomena similar to bulk strongly correlated materials, motivating the study of heavy-fermion physics in these systems.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo lattice model in moiré superlattices, exploring flat-band effects on Kondo screening.
result: They find that flat bands can drive a Kondo breakdown and lead to reentrant heavy-fermion behavior under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work reveals new aspects of heavy-fermion physics in moiré systems, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Orbital Magnetization Reveals Multiband Topology
authors: Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, And Wojciech J. Jankowski
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, and Wojciech J. Jankowski

We demonstrate that nontrivial multiband topological invariants of electronic wave functions can be revealed through orbital magnetization responses to external magnetic fields. We find that decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions allows one to deduce non…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235154] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that orbital magnetization responses can reveal multiband topological invariants in electronic systems.
motivation: To find a way to probe nontrivial multiband topology through measurable physical quantities.
method: Decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and analyzing its response to external magnetic fields.
result: The decomposition allows deduction of multiband topological invariants from orbital magnetization.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization is a useful probe for multiband topology, linking quantum geometry to observable responses.

title: Large Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Topological Hall Effect In The Kagome Helimagnet ${\mathrm{MgMn}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{6}$
authors: Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, And Wenhong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, and Wenhong Wang

Magnetic kagome materials have emerged as a new platform for exploring exotic topological transport phenomena. The anomalous Hall effect, a phenomenon prevalently observed in various magnetic kagome materials, is commonly explained using Berry-curvature concepts. Here we report that ${}…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect in the kagome helimagnet MgMn6Ge6, attributed to Berry curvature from the non-trivial spin texture.
motivation: To explore exotic topological transport phenomena in magnetic kagome materials, which are a platform for studying Berry-curvature-driven effects.
method: Synthesis of MgMn6Ge6 single crystals, measurement of Hall conductivity and magnetization, and analysis using Berry-curvature concepts.
result: Large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect are observed, linked to the non-trivial spin texture of the kagome lattice.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of Berry curvature in kagome helimagnets and suggest potential for spintronic applications.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism
authors: Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, And Haiyang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, and Haiyang Xu

Altermagnetism, characterized by pronounced momentum-space spin splitting without net magnetization, provides an emerging platform for spintronics. Yet nonvolatile control of its spin states remains a key challenge for device application. Here, we demonstrate that antiferroelastic lattice distortion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214457] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetic spin states via antiferroelastic lattice distortion.
motivation: Nonvolatile control of altermagnetism is crucial for spintronic device applications, but remains a key challenge.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to show that antiferroelastic distortion can switch the altermagnetic order parameter.
result: They find that strain-driven antiferroelastic switching enables reversible and nonvolatile control of spin splitting.
conclusion: This work provides a mechanism for electrically or mechanically controlling altermagnetic states, advancing spintronics.

title: Spin Transfer Torque Induced Deterministic Néel Vector Switching In Altermagnets
authors: Yuriy G. Semenov And Ki Wook Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yuriy G. Semenov and Ki Wook Kim

The process of spin-transfer torque in an altermagnet (AM) is theoretically investigated from the perspective of disparate effective exchange fields acting on the two sublattices. The momentum dependent, anisotropic spin splitting in the AM band structure can cause this asymmetry, leading ultimately…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224444] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates spin-transfer torque in altermagnets, focusing on Néel vector switching driven by anisotropic spin splitting.
motivation: Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials with potential for spintronic applications, and understanding spin-transfer torque in them is crucial for device development.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on the momentum-dependent anisotropic spin splitting in the altermagnet band structure to compute spin-transfer torque and its effect on the Néel vector.
result: They find that the asymmetric effective exchange fields on the two sublattices can induce deterministic Néel vector switching via spin-transfer torque.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using spin-transfer torque to control altermagnetic order, which may enable new spintronic devices.

title: Predicting Interface And Spin States In Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Junctions
authors: Sofia Sanz And Daniel Sánchez-Portal
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Sanz and Daniel Sánchez-Portal

We present a theoretical analysis of interface states emerging at junctions between armchair graphene nanoribbons of varying widths. By exploring diverse width combinations and junction geometries, we demonstrate that predicting the precise number of interface states requires considerations beyond t…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235434] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies interface states in armchair graphene nanoribbon junctions, focusing on electronic structure rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is important for nanoelectronics, but the work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform theoretical analysis using tight-binding or DFT calculations to predict interface states for various width combinations and geometries.
result: They find that predicting the number of interface states requires considerations beyond simple width matching.
conclusion: The study provides guidelines for engineering interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions, but has no relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Loss/gain-induced Hall Effect Of Vortex Light
authors: Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, And Kai Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, and Kai Chang

The Hall effect provides a route for unidirectional manipulations of classical and quantum waves. In optics, the spin Hall effect (SHE) induced by the interaction between intrinsic angular momentum (AM) and material inhomogeneity enables AM-dependent control of light at the subwavelength scale. Desp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245309] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a loss/gain-induced Hall effect for vortex light in optical systems, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To explore how non-Hermitian effects (loss/gain) can induce a Hall effect for optical vortices, extending the concept of spin Hall effect to orbital angular momentum.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the propagation of vortex light in a medium with loss/gain gradients, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and calculating the transverse deflection.
result: They predict a loss/gain-induced Hall effect where vortex light experiences a transverse shift proportional to the gradient of loss/gain and the topological charge.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for controlling light with orbital angular momentum using non-Hermitian optics, but it does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: First-principles Prediction Of A Multiferroic Semiconductor With Switchable Spin-polarized Berry Curvature Dipole: ${\mathrm{PbMnO}}_{3}$:${\mathrm{PbVO}}_{3}$
authors: Arpita Paul And Umesh V. Waghmare

tldr: First-principles prediction of a multiferroic semiconductor with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
motivation: To discover new multiferroic materials with coexisting ferromagnetism, ferroelectricity, and Berry curvature dipole for potential applications.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations and symmetry analysis.
result: The PbMnO3/PbVO3 superlattice is predicted to be a multiferroic with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
conclusion: This material may enable novel multifunctional devices, but the work is primarily a materials prediction without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, And Yu-Jun Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, and Yu-Jun Zhao

Two-dimensional unconventional magnetism has recently attracted growing interest due to its intriguing physical properties and promising applications in spintronics. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 214455] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a stacking theory for bilayer two-dimensional magnets to predict unconventional magnetism.
motivation: Existing studies on stacking-induced unconventional magnetism are limited to specific materials and configurations, lacking a general theoretical framework.
method: The authors propose a general stacking theory based on symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to classify and predict magnetic properties of bilayer 2D magnets.
result: The theory successfully explains known unconventional magnetic behaviors and predicts new ones in various bilayer systems.
conclusion: The stacking theory provides a systematic approach to engineer magnetism in bilayer 2D materials, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Antiferromagnetic Solitons In NiO As Possible Entities For Logic Operations
authors: Z. Li, T. Chirac, J. Tranchida, J.-Y. Chauleau, And M. Viret
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214456] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO for potential logic operations, focusing on spin wave and domain wall propagation.
motivation: To explore antiferromagnetic materials as a platform for high-speed logic devices using solitons.
method: Atomistic simulations of NiO stripes to model spin wave and domain wall propagation.
result: Demonstrates fast velocities over 40 km/s and interesting propagation properties enabling crossing of solitons.
conclusion: NiO stripes can serve as waveguides for antiferromagnetic solitons, potentially useful for logic operations.

title: Nontrivial Three-sublattice Magnetization In The Easy-axis Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Xxz Antiferromagnet On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, And Satoshi Nishimoto

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224442] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ground-state magnetic structure of an easy-axis spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on a triangular lattice using DMRG.
motivation: To understand the magnetic ordering in frustrated quantum magnets, specifically the triangular lattice antiferromagnet with easy-axis anisotropy.
method: Density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) with spiral boundary conditions to map finite clusters onto one-dimensional chains.
result: The ground state exhibits a nontrivial three-sublattice magnetization pattern.
conclusion: The easy-axis anisotropy stabilizes a three-sublattice magnetic order in the triangular lattice XXZ model.

title: Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo At The Basis Set Limit: Application To Lattice Constants
authors: Moritz Humer, Martin Schlipf, Zoran Sukurma, Sajad Bazrafshan, And Georg Kresse

tldr: This paper presents a plane-wave implementation of auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo within the PAW formalism in VASP for computing lattice constants.
motivation: Accurate computation of lattice constants from first principles is important for materials science, but existing methods are computationally expensive or limited in accuracy.
method: The authors implement AFQMC in VASP using plane-wave basis and PAW formalism, with exact inversion of the PAW overlap operator to maintain cubic scaling.
result: The method achieves basis set limit accuracy for lattice constants of several solids, demonstrating good agreement with experiment.
conclusion: The AFQMC implementation in VASP provides a practical and accurate tool for computing lattice constants and other ground-state properties of solids.

title: Orbital Hybridization Induces Giant Cubic Rashba Effect At The $\text{Cu/}{\mathrm{WO}}_{3}$ Interface
authors: Md Aktar Hossain And Saikat Das
abstract:
Author(s): Md Aktar Hossain and Saikat Das

Harnessing Rashba spin-orbit interaction and related spintronic functionalities has traditionally relied on metallic surfaces or interfaces containing elemental heavy metals. Here, using first-principles calculations and [MATH] as a model heterostructure, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235149] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the cubic Rashba effect at a Cu/WO3 interface using first-principles calculations, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: To explore orbital hybridization as a mechanism to induce a giant cubic Rashba effect without heavy metals, which is relevant for spintronics.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations are performed on the Cu/WO3 heterostructure to analyze the electronic structure and Rashba splitting.
result: A giant cubic Rashba effect is observed, attributed to orbital hybridization between Cu and WO3, with a large Rashba coefficient.
conclusion: Orbital hybridization at oxide interfaces can produce strong Rashba effects, offering a new route for spintronic materials without heavy elements.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:

Weyl exceptional lines typically occur in three-dimensional (3D) topological semimetals; however, they also emerge in the parameter space of one-dimensional (1D) systems. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 235150] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional rings in a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder, focusing on topological semimetal physics.
motivation: To understand the impact of dissipation on nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals using a 1D model.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model and compute its energy spectrum to identify exceptional rings.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D system due to dissipation.
conclusion: Dissipation can induce exceptional rings in lower-dimensional systems, extending the concept from 3D topological semimetals.

title: Taxonomy Of Integrable And Ground-state Solvable Models: Jastrow Wave Functions On Graphs And Parent Hamiltonians
authors: Nilanjan Sasmal And Adolfo Del Campo

motivation: To classify and construct exactly solvable many-body models with Jastrow-type wave functions on arbitrary graphs.
method: The authors define interactions via the adjacency matrix of a graph and derive parent Hamiltonians for which the Jastrow wave function is the ground state.
result: A taxonomy of integrable and ground-state solvable models is established, linking graph theory to many-body physics.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic framework for constructing solvable models, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Crossover In The Ordered Phase In The non-Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg Regime Of Spin Models With Long-range Coupling
authors: Jiewei Ding, Jiahao Su, Ho-Kin Tang, And Wing Chi Yu

tldr: This paper studies phase transitions and ordered phases in spin models with long-range interactions, focusing on the crossover behavior in the non-Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg regime.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between long-range interactions and thermal fluctuations in spin models is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics, with implications for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to analyze continuous spin models with power-law decaying interactions, examining the ordered phase and crossover phenomena.
result: They identify a crossover in the ordered phase that depends on the interaction range exponent, revealing new features beyond the Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg theorem.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase diagram of long-range spin systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics as defined in the research interests.

title: Quantized Dynamical Pumping Via Dissipation In A Mechanical Thouless Pump
authors: Marius Jürgensen And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064154] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantized dynamical pumping in a mechanical Thouless pump with dissipation, focusing on topological transport in classical systems.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects the quantized pumping of particles in a classical mechanical analog of the quantum Hall effect.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a mechanical Thouless pump model incorporating dissipation, using classical equations of motion and topological invariants.
result: They find that quantized pumping persists even in the presence of dissipation, with the pumped charge remaining integer quantized under certain conditions.
conclusion: Dissipation does not destroy the topological protection of quantized pumping in this classical system, extending the concept to non-Hermitian settings.

title: Quorum Sensing Promotes The Emergence Of Antifragile Regimes That Increase Bacterial Communities' Diversity
authors: Ivan Lechuga Jimenez And James Q. Boedicker

Author(s): Ivan Lechuga Jimenez and James Q. Boedicker

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064411] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how quorum sensing in bacterial communities promotes antifragile regimes that increase diversity, using a computational model.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition is important for ecology and evolution of microbial communities.
method: The authors develop a computational model of bacterial communities with quorum sensing and analyze the emergence of antifragile regimes and their effect on diversity.
result: Quorum sensing promotes antifragile regimes that increase bacterial community diversity.
conclusion: Quorum sensing can enhance community resilience and diversity through antifragile dynamics.

title: Approach To Network Failure Due To Intrinsic Fluctuations
authors: Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, And M. S. Santhanam

[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062302] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.

motivation: Understanding how intrinsic fluctuations in network nodes can lead to failure is important for network reliability.
method: The authors model flux as random walkers and node failure as extreme events, identifying three distinct failure regimes.
result: Three distinct nodal failure regimes are identified based on the statistics of fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for network failure due to intrinsic fluctuations, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Van Hove Singularities In The Density Of States Of A Chaotic Dynamical System
authors: Bryn Davies

Author(s): Bryn Davies

We show that the statistics of chaotic systems can be predicted by constructing an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computing their densities of states. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064211] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts chaotic system statistics using periodic differential operators and their density of states, revealing Van Hove singularities.
motivation: To understand the statistical properties of chaotic dynamical systems by linking them to well-understood periodic operators.
method: Constructs an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computes their densities of states.
result: The density of states exhibits Van Hove singularities, providing a new way to predict chaotic statistics.
conclusion: Chaotic systems can be analyzed via periodic operator theory, offering explicit predictions for their statistics.

title: Controlling Synchronization Dynamics Via Physics-informed Neural Networks
authors: Kaiming Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiming Luo

Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges. We propose a physics-informed neural network framework for continuous-time synchronization regulation, in which system trajectories and contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064212] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to control synchronization dynamics in networked systems.
motivation: Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges.
method: A physics-informed neural network framework is proposed for continuous-time synchronization regulation, incorporating system trajectories and control objectives into the loss function.
result: The framework enables precise control over synchronization timing and degree in simulated networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a flexible approach for synchronization control, with potential applications in complex networks.

title: Electronic Access To Glass Transition In Supercooled Ionic Liquids Using Ambipolar Transistor
authors: Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, And Subhadeep Datta

motivation: Conventional rheometry is incompatible with integrated electronic architectures, so a new electrical method is needed to study relaxation dynamics near the glass transition.
method: An ambipolar field-effect transistor is used to measure electrical transport in supercooled ionic liquids as a function of temperature.
result: The transistor detects changes in conductivity associated with the glass transition, providing an electronic signature of the dynamical arrest.
conclusion: The ambipolar transistor offers a viable electronic platform to study glass transition dynamics in supercooled ionic liquids.

title: Selective Wave Transmission In Strongly Nonlinear Disordered Granular Chains

motivation: Understanding wave propagation in disordered granular media is important for applications like impact mitigation and energy harvesting, but the paper focuses on classical mechanical systems without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Numerical simulations of 1000-granule chains with random radii following a normal distribution, subjected to striker impact or actuator-imposed band-limited white noise.
result: The disorder level controls selective wave transmission, with certain frequency components being transmitted or attenuated depending on the disorder strength.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into wave filtering in granular chains but have no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mode Coupling And Resonance-induced Relaxation In Carbon Nanotubes
authors: Hang Yu, Lin Deng, Weicheng Fu, Zhigang Zhu, Yisen Wang, And Liang Huang

tldr: This paper studies vibrational mode relaxation in carbon nanotubes, focusing on thermal transport and mechanical coherence.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional materials is important for thermal management and nanomechanical resonator design.
method: The authors investigate intrinsic relaxation of armchair CNTs under single-mode excitation using theoretical modeling and simulations.
result: They identify mode coupling and resonance-induced relaxation mechanisms that govern energy dissipation.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into thermal transport and coherence control in carbon nanotubes.

title: Robustness Of Networks Of Hypergraphs
authors: Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, And Jie Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, and Jie Zhou

Hypergraphs provide a natural representation of complex systems with higher-order interactions and are commonly interdependent with each other. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064312] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for networks of hypergraphs to study robustness against node failures.
motivation: Real-world systems often involve interdependent hypergraphs, but existing models do not capture such structures.
method: The authors represent hypergraphs as bipartite networks and define a network of hypergraphs (NOH) model, then analyze percolation and robustness.
result: They derive analytical conditions for the emergence of a giant connected component and find that interdependence can either enhance or reduce robustness depending on parameters.
conclusion: The NOH framework provides insights into the robustness of complex systems with higher-order interactions and interdependence.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Organic Mixed Conductors: Phase Transitions In A Lattice Gas
authors: Lukas M. Bongartz
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Bongartz

Organic mixed conductors (OMCs) represent a promising class of materials for applications in bioelectronics, physical computing, and thermoelectrics. tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in a lattice gas model for organic mixed conductors, focusing on statistical mechanics of coupled electronic, ionic, and mass transport.
motivation: Organic mixed conductors have applications in bioelectronics and thermoelectrics, but their complex multi-scale dynamics are not well understood.
method: The author develops a lattice gas model and applies statistical mechanics to analyze phase transitions in the coupled system.
result: The model predicts phase transitions driven by the interplay between electronic and ionic degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding transport in organic mixed conductors, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: First-passage Processes In A Deterministic One-dimensional Cellular Automaton Model Of Traffic Flow
authors: Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, And Eytan Katzav

result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a general characterization of noisy network dynamics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: The theory predicts accumulation and wetting transitions at repulsive barriers, with behavior depending on activity and barrier strength.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding active wetting, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper develops effective collective coordinate models for kink dynamics in a driven-damped φ^4 model.

title: Relations Among Different Inequality Measures In Complex Systems: From Kinetic Exchange To Earthquake Models
authors: Shohini Sen, Suchismita Banerjee, And Bikas K. Chakrabarti

We present a numerical study of several inequality measures across two kinetic wealth-exchange models with extreme inequality features (namely the Banerjee model, and the Chakraborti or yard-sale model) and two earthquake simulating models (namely the Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe two-fractal overlap mode…

motivation: To compare inequality measures across different complex systems (economic and geophysical) and explore universal features.
method: Numerical simulations of two kinetic wealth-exchange models (Banerjee and yard-sale) and two earthquake models (Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe and Olami-Feder-Christensen), computing Gini, Kolkata, and other indices.
result: Inequality measures show similar patterns across models, with the Kolkata index exhibiting a universal value near 0.8 at criticality.
conclusion: Inequality measures can reveal universal behavior in complex systems, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of A Fluctuation-driven Cooperative Solidlike Phase In Potts Model Monolayers

method: The authors perform Cellular Potts model simulations with different definitions of cell perimeter and area constraints, analyzing structural ordering and dynamics.
result: They identify a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase that emerges under certain conditions, distinct from previously known phases.
conclusion: The findings highlight the sensitivity of CPM simulations to implementation details and reveal a new phase behavior relevant to biological tissue modeling.

method: The authors prove that in the limit of structural balance, the Heider model with an external field maps exactly onto the Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions and no external field.
result: The signs of Heider relations that maintain structural equilibrium correspond to Ising spin configurations, establishing a direct equivalence.
conclusion: The equivalence provides a new perspective on social balance dynamics using tools from statistical mechanics, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: To assess the accuracy and applicability of truncated Wigner and positive-P representations for modeling light-matter interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
method: Uses the Jordan-Schwinger transformation to map atomic degrees of freedom and compares phase-space simulations with exact solutions for unitary and dissipative dynamics.
result: Identifies regimes where each method performs well and where they break down, providing guidelines for choosing the appropriate representation.
conclusion: Phase-space methods are useful for near-resonant propagation but require careful benchmarking to avoid inaccuracies in certain parameter regimes.

result: The formation and dynamics of the quantum Peregrine soliton are characterized, revealing correlations beyond mean-field.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum soliton dynamics but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-dimensional Aubry-André model with periodic twisting, likely using numerical simulations or analytical methods to study localization and topology.

motivation: Understanding how multiple swarms with different parameters and goals interact is important for biological, engineering, and defense applications.
method: The authors model two swarms moving in opposite directions and analyze their collision dynamics using agent-based simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They find that collisions can redirect swarms, leading to emergent patterns such as mixing, separation, or synchronized motion.
conclusion: Collision-mediated interactions can be exploited to control and redirect multiswarm systems.

result: They derive expressions for the Casimir-Polder potential on the excited atom, showing contributions from resonant and off-resonant processes.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed microscopic description of Casimir-Polder interactions in atomic arrays, which could be important for quantum simulation and sensing platforms.

tldr: This paper presents a high-stability optical clock based on a continuously ground-state cooled Al+ ion, achieving reduced averaging time without compromising accuracy.
motivation: Single-ion optical clocks have high systematic accuracy but require long averaging times to reach statistical uncertainty; this work aims to reduce that time without sacrificing accuracy.
method: The authors implement continuous ground-state cooling of an Al+ ion to enable longer probe times while mitigating time-dilation shifts, and characterize the clock's stability and accuracy.
result: The clock achieves a fractional frequency instability below 10^-15 at 1 second and a systematic uncertainty at the 10^-18 level, with significantly reduced averaging time compared to previous single-ion clocks.
conclusion: Continuous ground-state cooling allows single-ion optical clocks to combine high accuracy with high stability, making them more practical for precision timekeeping applications.

result: The framework successfully identifies topological phases in amorphous higher-order topological insulators, demonstrating the mode-shell correspondence in a broader context.
conclusion: The one-particle density matrix provides a robust tool for topological characterization in disordered systems, extending the applicability of the mode-shell correspondence.

method: The authors employ a quantum-optical approach treating both the driving field and the atomic system quantum mechanically, deriving an effective Hamiltonian and solving the dynamics.
result: They show that HHG can occur even with zero mean field due to quantum fluctuations, and predict distinct features in the harmonic spectrum compared to classical driving.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for HHG with quantum light, opening up new possibilities for strong-field physics and attosecond science.

abstract:

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experimental demonstrations.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a theoretical gap.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic arguments and hardness proofs tailored to the saturated regime of BosonSampling with linear mode counts.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in this regime remains classically hard under plausible conjectures, providing theoretical support for current experiments.
conclusion: The work validates the quantum advantage claims of near-term photonic experiments by extending the theoretical foundation to experimentally relevant parameter regimes.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
motivation: To understand the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains and their experimental signatures.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: These solitons are detectable via inelastic neutron scattering, providing a way to observe quantum soliton dynamics.

abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs numerically.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such theories.

result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based information manipulation.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures for potential applications in information processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature

abstract:

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for engineering robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler

tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks based on observed dynamics.
method: The authors propose a physics-informed framework that leverages dynamical equations to infer causal interactions.
result: The framework successfully infers causal links across a range of networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a general tool for network inference with potential applications in various fields.

authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transition of the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel magnetic phase transition in a kagome spin ice, contributing to the understanding of frustrated magnetism.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but typically require low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe orbital-selective flat bands that persist up to room temperature, with tunability via chemical composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated electron physics and potential applications in quantum devices at ambient conditions.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and evaluate the effectiveness of standard heat treatments.
result: They find that silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The discovery of persistent anisotropy suggests that alternative deposition and postprocessing methods are needed to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of a model of spinning particles that form a hyperuniform fluid.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal new critical phenomena in hyperuniform systems, relevant to soft matter physics.

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different types of ferroic orders and the formation of complex domain walls in a material with a uniform ferro-rotational state.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to study the material Ni2MnSe2O3.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state that couples polarity and chirality was identified, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders.

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.

tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show unexpected scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and provide insights into wave dynamics in disordered systems.

abstract:

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.

tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, meaning domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that the thermodynamic limit is independent of boundary conditions or domain shape in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries and analyze ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not be universally valid in quantum spin and dimer models, with implications for understanding quantum phase transitions and ground state selection.
