title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid evolution of the field, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a vibrant field with many open directions for fundamental physics and applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electronic states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in complex systems like ecology and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across different fields.
method: Uses field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism) to derive and solve master equations for reaction-diffusion processes.
result: Provides a unified framework that connects chemical reaction kinetics, ecology, and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To update the field of spin glasses and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and simulation results on spin-glass dynamics.
result: Summarizes progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary work is needed.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity in the brain.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity to enable perception, thought, and action is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to quantitative recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural activity, demonstrating predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for bridging theory and experiment in neuroscience, revealing emergent properties of neural networks.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models that describe internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical approaches and an outlook on their incorporation into application-oriented studies.
conclusion: The authors conclude that these theoretical methods can be useful for advancing photonics and energy harvesting technologies.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights quantum effects such as tunneling, superposition, and entanglement in skyrmion systems, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new functionalities in quantum technologies, but further research is needed to realize practical applications.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review compiles current constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, highlighting the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further experimental improvements and theoretical developments are needed.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from assumptions not being met.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why is important for materials science.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and circumstances where bounds are exceeded, analyzing which underlying assumptions are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, homogeneity), and shows how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds do not contradict thermodynamics but rather highlight the importance of assumptions; this knowledge can guide development of materials with extreme properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing nonstandard geometries in synthetic quantum matter.
result: Summarizes progress in engineering fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems across multiple platforms.
conclusion: These synthetic geometries open new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics and simulating fundamental theories.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework for self-alignment.
result: Self-alignment leads to novel phenomena such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter that can inspire new discoveries and applications.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of experimental and theoretical efforts to probe gravity using massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested fundamental force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., collapse models, gravitationally induced entanglement) and experimental platforms (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics).
result: Current experiments are approaching the sensitivity needed to test gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement, but no definitive quantum gravity signature has been observed.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to study the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: High-$Q$ Nonlocal Resonances In Mirror-Enhanced Plasmonic Lattices
authors: Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, And Xianyu Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, and Xianyu Ao

Plasmonic nanoparticle arrays stand as a versatile platform for enhancing light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. Ultrahigh-quality-factor (high-[MATH]) resonances are critical for spectrally selective applications such as label-free biosensing, low-threshold lasing, and quantum information process…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016901] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-quality-factor nonlocal resonances in mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices for enhancing light-matter interactions.
motivation: Ultrahigh-Q resonances are critical for applications like biosensing, lasing, and quantum information processing, but achieving them in plasmonic lattices is challenging.
method: The authors propose a mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice design that supports nonlocal resonances with high Q-factors, analyzed theoretically and numerically.
result: They demonstrate that the mirror configuration significantly boosts the Q-factor of nonlocal resonances, achieving values suitable for practical applications.
conclusion: Mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices provide a promising platform for high-Q nanophotonic devices, with potential in sensing and quantum technologies.

title: General-Purpose Inverse Design Of Heterogeneous Finite-Sized Assemblies
authors: Livia A. J. Guttieres, Ryan K. Krueger, Remi Drolet, And Michael P. Brenner
abstract:
Author(s): Livia A. J. Guttieres, Ryan K. Krueger, Remi Drolet, and Michael P. Brenner

Designing heterogeneous, self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology. We present a framework that uses gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, tuning systems toward target equilibrium yields. We design systems ranging from simple dimers to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018201] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a gradient-based optimization framework for inverse design of heterogeneous self-assembling systems to achieve target equilibrium yields.
motivation: Designing heterogeneous self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology, and existing methods lack general-purpose inverse design capabilities.
method: The authors use gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, tuning system parameters toward target equilibrium yields.
result: The framework is demonstrated on systems ranging from simple dimers to more complex assemblies, achieving target yields.
conclusion: The approach provides a general-purpose method for inverse design of heterogeneous finite-sized assemblies, with potential applications in soft matter and biology.

title: Block-Type Antiferromagnetism In Single Chain Quasi-One-Dimensional ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$
authors: Fei Gao, Nikhil Dhale, Ling-Fang Lin, Keith M. Taddei, Yang Zhang, Clarina Dela Cruz, Elbio Dagotto, And Bing Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Gao, Nikhil Dhale, Ling-Fang Lin, Keith M. Taddei, Yang Zhang, Clarina Dela Cruz, Elbio Dagotto, and Bing Lv

One-dimensional (1D) structures provide a unique platform to study the correlated quantum interactions and phase transitions such as unconventional magnetism and superconducting states. Here, we report that iron chalcogenide [MATH] exhibits an unusual bl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256706] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports an unusual block-type antiferromagnetic order in a quasi-1D iron chalcogenide, studied via neutron scattering and DFT.
motivation: One-dimensional structures are a platform for studying correlated quantum interactions and unconventional magnetism; the specific compound K3Fe2Se4 was expected to exhibit interesting magnetic behavior.
method: Single-crystal neutron diffraction and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to determine the magnetic structure and electronic properties.
result: The material exhibits a block-type antiferromagnetic order with ferromagnetically aligned Fe dimers antiferromagnetically coupled along the chain, and a large magnetic moment of ~3.5 μB/Fe.
conclusion: The discovery of block antiferromagnetism in a quasi-1D system provides a new platform for studying low-dimensional magnetism and its interplay with electronic correlations.

title: Extreme Confinement Of Hydrogen Gas Within Fullerenelike Nanoporous Carbon
authors: Callum L. Wood, Adam J. C. Singor, Nigel A. Marks, Mark Paskevicius, Craig E. Buckley, And Jacob W. Martin
abstract:
Author(s): Callum L. Wood, Adam J. C. Singor, Nigel A. Marks, Mark Paskevicius, Craig E. Buckley, and Jacob W. Martin

Nanoporous carbons and carbon nanostructures can store hydrogen at cryogenic temperatures but lack the volumetric and gravimetric capacity to be industrially significant. Recent inelastic neutron scattering experiments suggest a highly dense phase of hydrogen at temperatures well above the melting p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245429] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hydrogen confinement in nanoporous carbon, focusing on material science and hydrogen storage, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the extreme confinement of hydrogen gas in nanoporous carbon and its potential for hydrogen storage.
method: Computational simulations and analysis of hydrogen behavior in fullerenelike nanoporous carbon structures.
result: The study reveals a highly dense phase of hydrogen at temperatures above the melting point, confined within the nanopores.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into hydrogen storage in carbon nanostructures but do not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Giant Field-free Transverse Josephson Diode Effect In Altermagnets
authors: Bijay Kumar Sahoo And Abhiram Soori
abstract:
Author(s): Bijay Kumar Sahoo and Abhiram Soori

We predict a field-free transverse Josephson diode effect in altermagnets (AMs) with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, achieving diode efficiencies exceeding [MATH] and unidirectional transverse supercurrents in four-terminal junctions. In this geometry, a longitudinal phase bias generates transverse sup…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245433] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts a field-free transverse Josephson diode effect in altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, achieving high diode efficiencies.
motivation: To explore the Josephson diode effect in altermagnets, which could enable novel superconducting devices without external magnetic fields.
method: The authors theoretically model a four-terminal Josephson junction with altermagnet and Rashba spin-orbit coupling, calculating supercurrents and diode efficiencies.
result: They find a field-free transverse Josephson diode effect with efficiencies exceeding 100% and unidirectional transverse supercurrents.
conclusion: Altermagnets with Rashba coupling can host a strong transverse Josephson diode effect, offering potential for superconducting electronics.

title: Nonthermal Melting And Density Wave Instability Coupled To The Lattice In ${\mathrm{La}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10}$
authors: Chen Zhang, Lixing Chen, Qi-Yi Wu, Congcong Le, Xianxin Wu, Hao Liu, Bo Chen, Ying Zhou, Zhong-Tuo Fu, Chun-Hui Lv, Zi-Jie Xu, Hai-Long Deng, Enkang Zhang, Yinghao Zhu, H. Y. Liu, Yu-Xia Duan, Jun Zhao, And Jian-Qiao Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Chen Zhang, Lixing Chen, Qi-Yi Wu, Congcong Le, Xianxin Wu, Hao Liu, Bo Chen, Ying Zhou, Zhong-Tuo Fu, Chun-Hui Lv, Zi-Jie Xu, Hai-Long Deng, Enkang Zhang, Yinghao Zhu, H. Y. Liu, Yu-Xia Duan, Jun Zhao, and Jian-Qiao Meng

The recent discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in pressurized nickelates has renewed interest in the broken-symmetry states of their ambient-pressure parent phases, where a density wave (DW) order emerges and competes with superconductivity, but its microscopic origin remains unresolved.…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241121] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonthermal melting and density wave instability in La4Ni3O10, a nickelate material, using pump-probe spectroscopy and DFT calculations.
motivation: To understand the microscopic origin of density wave order in pressurized nickelates, which competes with high-temperature superconductivity.
method: Time-resolved reflectivity measurements and first-principles calculations to probe lattice dynamics and electronic structure.
result: Observation of nonthermal melting of the density wave order and a lattice instability coupled to the density wave.
conclusion: The density wave in La4Ni3O10 is driven by electron-phonon coupling and lattice effects, providing insight into the parent phase of superconducting nickelates.

title: Bistable Fourth Sound Resonance In Superfluid $^{3}\mathrm{He}\text{−}\mathrm{B}$ Due To Gap Suppression
authors: Alexander J. Shook, Daksh Malhotra, Aymar Muhikira, And John P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander J. Shook, Daksh Malhotra, Aymar Muhikira, and John P. Davis

Superfluidity in [MATH] exhibits many unique properties that are of interest to modern condensed matter research, including multiple superfluid phase transitions, topological defects, and exotic classes of excitations like Majorana and Weyl fermions. Many of the most interesting theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214519] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistable fourth sound resonance in superfluid 3He-B due to gap suppression, a condensed matter phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear acoustic effects in superfluid 3He-B, which exhibits topological defects and exotic excitations.
method: Experimental measurement of fourth sound resonance in a superfluid 3He-B cavity, analyzing bistability caused by superfluid gap suppression.
result: Observed bistable resonance behavior attributed to the suppression of the superfluid gap by the sound field.
conclusion: The bistable fourth sound resonance provides insight into nonlinear dynamics in superfluid 3He-B, relevant to condensed matter physics.

title: Vibrational And Diffusional Thermal Transport In Amorphous And Deeply Supercooled Liquid Alumina
authors: Honggang Zhang, Xiaoyi Chen, Yangshun Lan, Changchun Ding, Dingbo Zhang, Yuxiang Ni, And Hua Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Honggang Zhang, Xiaoyi Chen, Yangshun Lan, Changchun Ding, Dingbo Zhang, Yuxiang Ni, and Hua Bao

Thermal transport in amorphous materials involves a complex interplay between anharmonicity and atomic-scale dynamics, particularly across the glass transition. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, we investigate the temperature dependence of thermal transport in amorphous ${}_{2}{\mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224318] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal transport in amorphous and supercooled liquid alumina, focusing on vibrational and diffusional contributions.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in amorphous materials is important for applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations and theoretical analysis of heat transport mechanisms.
result: Identifies temperature-dependent contributions from vibrations and atomic diffusion to thermal conductivity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermal transport in disordered materials but lacks relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, and Matthew E. Potter

Isotopic substitution modifies nuclear masses without altering the electronic potential-energy surface to first order and is therefore often interpreted as a simple rescaling of vibrational frequencies. In solids with dense phonon manifolds, however, mass substitution acts as a parametric Hermitian …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotope substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, focusing on collective mixing effects.
motivation: To understand the impact of mass substitution on vibrational properties beyond simple frequency rescaling, particularly in dense phonon manifolds.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze parametric Hermitian perturbations due to mass changes and their effect on phonon eigenvectors.
result: Isotope substitution induces collective phonon mixing and eigenvector transport, altering mode localization and transport properties.
conclusion: Mass substitution in solids with dense phonon spectra leads to nontrivial changes in phonon dynamics that go beyond frequency shifts.

title: Strongly Quenched Kramers Doublet Magnetism In ${\mathrm{SmMgAl}}_{11}{\mathrm{O}}_{19}$
authors: Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, And Ross H. Colman
abstract:
Author(s): Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, and Ross H. Colman

We report magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements on the rare-earth hexaaluminate [MATH], where [MATH] realizes a strongly quenched Kramers doublet on a triangular lattice with an exceptionally weak net exchan…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224443] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental measurements of magnetic susceptibility, magnetization, and specific heat on a rare-earth hexaaluminate compound, revealing strongly quenched Kramers doublet magnetism on a triangular lattice.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of SmMgAl11O19, a rare-earth hexaaluminate with a triangular lattice, and characterize its low-energy magnetic behavior.
method: Magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements were performed on single-crystal or polycrystalline samples.
result: The system exhibits a strongly quenched Kramers doublet with exceptionally weak net exchange interactions.
conclusion: The compound provides a platform for studying frustrated magnetism in a triangular lattice with minimal exchange coupling.

title: Spin-dependent Orbital Selectivity And Partial Kondo-like Screening In The Magnetically Ordered Hund's Metal ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoO}}_{4}$
authors: Shivani Bhardwaj And Sudhir K. Pandey
abstract:
Author(s): Shivani Bhardwaj and Sudhir K. Pandey

Hund's metallicity in [MATH] transition metal oxides constitutes a rare class of compounds, since they have been long understood considering the dominance of Hubbard [MATH]. [MATH] belong to this rare class of metals; among them,…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235147] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-dependent orbital selectivity and Kondo-like screening in the magnetically ordered Hund's metal Sr2CoO4 using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and correlation effects in Hund's metals, which are rare and not fully understood.
method: First-principles DFT+DMFT calculations with continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo impurity solver.
result: Orbital-selective behavior and partial Kondo-like screening are observed in the magnetically ordered state.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the interplay of spin, orbital, and charge degrees of freedom in Hund's metals.

title: Quasiparticle Interference In LiFeAs: Signature Of Inelastic Tunneling Through Spin Fluctuations
authors: Shun Chi, Carolina A. Marques, W. N. Hardy, Ruixing Liang, Pinder Dosanjh, D. A. Bonn, S. A. Burke, And Peter Wahl
abstract:
Author(s): Shun Chi, Carolina A. Marques, W. N. Hardy, Ruixing Liang, Pinder Dosanjh, D. A. Bonn, S. A. Burke, and Peter Wahl

Quasiparticle interference (QPI) is a powerful tool to characterize the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in unconventional superconductors, by mapping the spatial dependence of elastic tunneling of electrons between the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope and a sample. Here, we con…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235148] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle interference in the iron-based superconductor LiFeAs, focusing on inelastic tunneling through spin fluctuations.
motivation: Understanding the pairing mechanism in unconventional superconductors is a key goal; quasiparticle interference can reveal the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter.
method: Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) is used to map quasiparticle interference patterns, and the data are analyzed to distinguish elastic from inelastic tunneling contributions.
result: The observed quasiparticle interference patterns are consistent with inelastic tunneling mediated by spin fluctuations, providing insight into the pairing mechanism.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that inelastic tunneling via spin fluctuations plays a significant role in quasiparticle interference in LiFeAs, which may inform models of superconductivity in iron-based materials.

title: Stochastic Search With Space-dependent Diffusivity
authors: Hwai-Ray Tung And Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Hwai-Ray Tung and Sean D. Lawley

The canonical model of stochastic search tracks a randomly diffusing “searcher” until it finds a “target.” Owing to its many applications across science and engineering, this perennially popular problem has been thoroughly investigated in a variety of models. However, aside from some exactly solvabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064149] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic search with space-dependent diffusivity, a problem in statistical physics and applied mathematics.
motivation: Understanding how a diffusing searcher finds a target in heterogeneous environments is important for many applications, but exact solutions are rare.

result: They find that the stronger ferromagnetic exchange interactions in Fe3GaTe2, due to the larger atomic size of Ga, lead to a higher Curie temperature.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical explanation for the observed Curie temperature difference and suggests that substituting Ge with larger atoms can enhance magnetic ordering temperature.

title: Angular Anisotropy Landscape Of Vortex Ensembles In Polarized Small-angle Neutron Scattering
authors: Michael P. Adams, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, And Andreas Michels
abstract:
Author(s): Michael P. Adams, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, and Andreas Michels

We present a symmetry-resolved classification of two-dimensional spin-flip small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) patterns arising from dilute ensembles of spherical nanoparticles hosting magnetic vortex states. Based on a linear vortex ansatz with an axially symmetric distribution of vortex axes and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023328] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper classifies small-angle neutron scattering patterns from magnetic vortex ensembles in nanoparticles.
motivation: Understanding the angular anisotropy of SANS patterns from vortex states is important for characterizing magnetic nanostructures.
method: The authors use a linear vortex ansatz with axially symmetric distribution of vortex axes to compute spin-flip SANS cross sections.
result: They provide a symmetry-resolved classification of two-dimensional SANS patterns for dilute ensembles of spherical nanoparticles with magnetic vortices.
conclusion: The classification aids in interpreting experimental SANS data from vortex ensembles.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally tracks ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using ultrafast electron diffraction.
motivation: To directly observe and characterize ion diffusion in superionic conductors at ultrafast timescales, linking microscopic dynamics to macroscopic properties.
method: Ultrafast electron diffraction with pump-probe techniques to capture structural changes during ion diffusion.
result: Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion dynamics in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: The approach provides a better understanding of ion transport in superionic conductors, aiding material design.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on glass stability effects.
motivation: Understanding the relationship between glass stability and low-frequency vibrations is important for glass physics but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique was used to measure vibrational properties of vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: The study clarifies how glass stability influences low-frequency vibrational modes.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of glass dynamics but are unrelated to the specified research directions.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the interplay of surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators, fusion reactors, and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques.
result: Applications include trapping, manipulation, sorting, and pulling forces on particles.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in biophysics, nanotechnology, and particle manipulation.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and material properties.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit interesting localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper is a review summarizing experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of the unique behavior of these materials, including changes in electronic structure and bonding under pressure.
conclusion: The reviewed work expands understanding of transplutonium materials, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the multimessenger implications for astrophysics.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, and understanding their detection prospects and multimessenger connections is important for advancing our knowledge of dense matter and neutron star physics.
method: The paper reviews the current status and future capabilities of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the role of simultaneous electromagnetic observations in multimessenger astronomy.
result: It outlines the detection prospects for continuous waves in upcoming detector generations and surveys the potential astrophysical implications.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations combining gravitational and electromagnetic waves will significantly enhance our understanding of neutron star interiors and related astrophysical processes.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars.
method: Review of gravitational-wave and X-ray observations, compared to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized.
conclusion: Future observations will further constrain the equation of state.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond Standard Model physics, but recent experimental bounds have narrowed the viable parameter space, motivating a survey of remaining possibilities.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels for the HL-LHC.
result: The paper provides an overview of the status of supersymmetry and outlines the discovery potential of the HL-LHC for various supersymmetric scenarios.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable but highly constrained; the HL-LHC will be crucial for testing the remaining parameter space.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the broader perspective of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and the evolution of his thinking in physics, particularly regarding neural networks.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture, not a technical research paper.
result: No new scientific results; a retrospective on past contributions.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that can be applied broadly, including to artificial intelligence.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics, but direct measurements are often impossible due to extremely low cross sections.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques to study these reactions.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical models and experimental methods for low-energy nuclear reactions in stars.
conclusion: The review highlights the need for continued theoretical and experimental efforts to better understand stellar nucleosynthesis and energy generation.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates incorporate new measurements and improved uncertainties.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties.
result: A self-consistent set of values for the fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, with updated uncertainties.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values supersede previous sets and serve as the internationally recommended reference for fundamental constants.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image biological tissues.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy can image millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, providing optical contrast in biological tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advancements in multimodal approaches.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with applications in materials science and biology.
motivation: Understanding the formation of creases and cusps during buckling of soft materials is important for morphogenesis and swelling of gels.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and explains how nonlinear elasticity captures crease and cusp formation.
conclusion: Nonlinear elasticity theory is essential for a complete understanding of buckling patterns in soft matter.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses gravitational wave signals from the early universe, including phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves offer a unique probe of the first second of the universe, as they are not blocked by the primordial plasma.
method: The paper reviews theoretical predictions for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from cosmological sources and detection strategies.
result: It summarizes potential signals from phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe phenomena.
conclusion: Gravitational waves can reveal information about the earliest moments of the universe, complementing electromagnetic and neutrino observations.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools for constructing and using Wannier functions in condensed-matter physics.
method: The paper surveys the ecosystem of software packages that implement Wannier-function approaches, describing their capabilities and interoperability.
result: The review catalogs the major software tools and their applications, highlighting the widespread use of Wannier functions in electronic structure calculations.
conclusion: The Wannier-function software ecosystem is a major instrument for understanding and designing materials, with broad applications in condensed-matter physics.

title: Observation Of $\mathrm{Ξ}(1530{)}^{0}$ Polarization And Determination Of Its Electric And Magnetic Moments In $ψ(3686)→\mathrm{Ξ}(1530{)}^{0}\overline{\mathrm{Ξ}}(1530{)}^{0}$
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

tldr: This paper reports the observation of Ξ(1530)0 polarization and determination of its electric and magnetic moments in ψ(3686) decays using BESIII data.
motivation: To measure the polarization and electromagnetic moments of the Ξ(1530)0 baryon, which are important for understanding its internal structure and strong interaction dynamics.
method: Analysis of ψ(3686)→Ξ(1530)0‾Ξ(1530)0 decays using a data sample of (2.7±0.1)×10^9 ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector.
result: First observation of Ξ(1530)0 polarization with significance >5σ, and determination of its electric and magnetic moments.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into baryon structure and test theoretical predictions from lattice QCD and chiral perturbation theory.

title: Multifaceted Decay Of $^{116}\mathrm{Cs}$
authors: J. Dey, U. Datta, O. Tengblad, P. Das, A. Rahaman, B. K. Agrawal, S. Chakraborty, A. Gottberg, M. Kowalska, K. Mahata, S. Mandal, M. Madurga, E. Nacher, E. Rapisarda, N. Warr, W. Sengupta, C. Sharma, And T. Stora
abstract:
Author(s): J. Dey, U. Datta, O. Tengblad, P. Das, A. Rahaman, B. K. Agrawal, S. Chakraborty, A. Gottberg, M. Kowalska, K. Mahata, S. Mandal, M. Madurga, E. Nacher, E. Rapisarda, N. Warr, W. Sengupta, C. Sharma, and T. Stora

The multifaceted decay properties of [MATH] near the proton drip line have been studied at ISOLDE, CERN. More than six new unbound states of [MATH] have been identified. A novel phenomenon of low energy isoscalar octupole resonance has been observed. After proton decay, tha…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 012501] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decay properties of 116Cs near the proton drip line, identifying new unbound states and observing low-energy isoscalar octupole resonance.
motivation: To understand the multifaceted decay of 116Cs and explore nuclear structure near the proton drip line.
method: Experimental study at ISOLDE, CERN, using proton decay and gamma-ray spectroscopy.
result: More than six new unbound states of 116Cs were identified, and a low-energy isoscalar octupole resonance was observed.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into nuclear structure and decay modes near the proton drip line.

title: Elinvar Effect By Nanoscale Displacive Phase Transformation In Martensites
authors: Die Liu, Yao Liu, Junming Gou, Tianyu Ma, And Xiaobing Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Die Liu, Yao Liu, Junming Gou, Tianyu Ma, and Xiaobing Ren

Ferroelastic alloys suffer modulus softening prior to the martensitic transformation, but still exhibit normal cooling-hardening effect below the martensitic transformation finish temperature, [MATH]. Here we report an unprecedented phenomenon that a martensitic state can show nearly tem…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016101] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports an elinvar effect in martensites due to nanoscale displacive phase transformation.
motivation: Ferroelastic alloys typically show modulus softening before martensitic transformation and normal cooling-hardening below it; the authors discovered an unprecedented nearly temperature-independent modulus (elinvar effect) in a martensitic state.
method: Experimental study using a specific alloy composition and characterization techniques to measure elastic modulus as a function of temperature.
result: The martensitic state exhibits a nearly temperature-independent elastic modulus over a wide temperature range.
conclusion: The elinvar effect arises from nanoscale displacive phase transformation, offering potential for applications requiring stable elastic properties.

title: Transient Large-Scale Anisotropy In TeV Cosmic Rays Due To An Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejection
authors: Zhen Cao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Cao et al. (LHAASO Collaboration)

A solar storm hitting Earth appears to have reduced the amount of incoming high-energy cosmic rays, suggesting a new way of measuring solar activity.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251002] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of transient large-scale anisotropy in TeV cosmic rays caused by an interplanetary coronal mass ejection, using data from the LHAASO observatory.
motivation: Understanding how solar activity affects high-energy cosmic rays can provide new insights into solar physics and space weather.
method: The LHAASO Collaboration analyzed data from their observatory to measure the anisotropy of TeV cosmic rays during a solar storm event.
result: They observed a reduction in incoming high-energy cosmic rays and a transient large-scale anisotropy correlated with the interplanetary coronal mass ejection.
conclusion: This suggests a new method for measuring solar activity using cosmic ray observations.

title: Pattern Formation During Melting Of Lamellar Eutectics
authors: Rahul Nellissery Rajan, Rajesh Kumari Rajendran, Guillaume Boussinot, Kamal Sbargoud, Sabine Bottin-Rousseau, And Silvère Akamatsu
abstract:
Author(s): Rahul Nellissery Rajan, Rajesh Kumari Rajendran, Guillaume Boussinot, Kamal Sbargoud, Sabine Bottin-Rousseau, and Silvère Akamatsu

A rich diversity of patterns emerge during melting of a two-phase eutectic solid.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256301] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pattern formation during melting of lamellar eutectics, a topic in materials science and solidification physics.
motivation: Understanding pattern formation in eutectic melting is important for controlling material microstructure, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: Experimental observation and theoretical modeling of melting dynamics in two-phase eutectic solids.
result: A rich diversity of patterns emerge during melting, which are characterized and analyzed.
conclusion: The study provides insights into pattern formation in eutectic systems but has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Search For Dark Matter Induced Airglow In Planetary Atmospheres
authors: Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, And Joshua Tong
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, and Joshua Tong

We point out that dark matter (DM) can illuminate planetary skies via ultraviolet airglow. Dark matter annihilation products can excite molecular hydrogen, which then deexcites to produce ultraviolet emission in the Lyman and Werner bands. We search for this new effect by analyzing nightside ultravi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251001] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes that dark matter annihilation in planetary atmospheres can produce ultraviolet airglow, and searches for this signal in planetary data.
motivation: Dark matter detection is a major goal in physics, and this work explores a new indirect detection channel using planetary atmospheres as targets.
method: The authors model dark matter annihilation products exciting molecular hydrogen, leading to UV emission in Lyman and Werner bands, and analyze nightside ultraviolet observations of planets.
result: They report constraints on dark matter annihilation cross-sections from the absence of observed airglow.
conclusion: Planetary atmospheres can serve as novel detectors for dark matter, and this method provides competitive limits on certain dark matter models.

title: Short Strings In Three-Dimensional Anti–de Sitter Space: From Weak To Strong Coupling
authors: Simon Ekhammar, Nikolay Gromov, Bogdan Stefański, Jr., And Charles Thull
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Ekhammar, Nikolay Gromov, Bogdan Stefański, Jr., and Charles Thull

We numerically solve the conjectured quantum spectral curve for strings on [MATH] with Ramond-Ramond charge from weak to strong coupling. At strong coupling, the spectrum organizes into flat-space string mass levels with universal square-root s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251603] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the quantum spectral curve for strings in AdS3 with Ramond-Ramond charge, studying the spectrum from weak to strong coupling.

result: The FM-MCMC algorithm demonstrates improved sampling efficiency and accuracy compared to traditional MCMC methods on synthetic and real exoplanet data.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a more efficient approach for estimating orbital parameters, which could be useful for analyzing direct imaging exoplanet data.

title: Proof-of-principle Experiment Of A Beam Extraction Over Millions Of Turns Using Stable Resonance Islands And Bent Crystal
authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. tldr: This paper reports a proof-of-principle experiment on beam extraction using stable resonance islands and a bent crystal at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron.
motivation: To develop a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators.
method: Combined particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber.
result: Successful demonstration of beam extraction over millions of turns using the proposed technique.
conclusion: The method offers a promising option for low-loss slow extraction in high-energy accelerators.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and demonstrates its application to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by achieving a broadband out-of-phase response.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, showing that a resonant system can maintain a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth. They apply this to flow control.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications, breaking the traditional bandwidth limit of resonant modes.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and beyond.
